title.zh: 卷一百〇七 列傳第四十五: 高汝礪 張行信
title.en: Volume 107 Biographies 45: Gao Ruli, Zhang Xingxin
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 列傳第四十五: 高汝礪 張行信 Volume 107 Biographies 45: Gao Ruli, Zhang Xingxin

sentences.zh: 高汝礪

translations.literal: Gao Ruli
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli

sentences.zh: 高汝礪，字岩夫，應州金城人。

translations.literal: Gao Ruli, style name Yanfu, was a native of Jincheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli, whose style name was Yanfu, came from Jincheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登大定十九年進士第，蒞官有能聲。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of Dading and gained a reputation for competence in office.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the nineteenth year of the Dading reign (1179) and soon earned a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年九月，章宗詔宰執，舉奏中外可為刺史者，上親閱闕點注，蓋取兩員同舉者升用之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Mingchang, Emperor Zhangzong ordered the chief ministers to submit nominations from within and outside the court of those fit to serve as prefects; the emperor personally reviewed and marked the roster, generally promoting those whom two officials had jointly recommended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Mingchang (1194), Zhangzong instructed his chief ministers to nominate candidates inside and outside the court for prefectural posts. He personally reviewed the lists and marked his choices, generally elevating only those whom two nominators had named in common.

sentences.zh: 於是，汝礪自同知絳陽軍節度事起為石州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruli was promoted from Vice Commissioner of the Jinyang Military Commission to Prefect of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis Ruli rose from deputy commissioner on the Jinyang military commission to prefect of Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 承安元年七月，入為左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Cheng'an, he entered the capital as Left Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Cheng'an (1196) he was appointed director in the left bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 一日奏事紫宸殿，時侍臣皆回避，上所禦涼扇忽墮案下，汝礪以非職不敢取以進。

translations.literal: One day while presenting business in the Zichen Hall, when all attending officials had withdrawn, the cool fan the emperor was using suddenly fell to the desk; Ruli, deeming it outside his duty, did not dare pick it up and present it.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was reporting to the throne in the Zichen Hall while the attending staff had been sent out of earshot. The emperor's hand fan slipped onto the desk; Ruli, judging that retrieval was not his office, did not pick it up and offer it back.

sentences.zh: 奏事畢，上謂宰臣曰：「高汝礪不進扇，可謂知體矣。」

translations.literal: When he had finished his report, the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Gao Ruli did not present the fan—he may be said to understand propriety."
translations.idiomatic: After the audience the emperor told his chief ministers, "Gao Ruli left the fan where it fell—he clearly understands his proper bounds."

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was raised to remonstrating grand master on the left.

sentences.zh: 以賦調軍須，郡縣有司或不得人，追胥走卒利其事急，規取貨賂，深為民害，建言：「自今若因兵調發，有犯者乞權依'推排受財法'治之，庶使小人有所畏懼。」

translations.literal: Because levies for military supplies were being collected, county and prefectural officials sometimes failed to appoint the right men; pursuing clerks and runners took advantage of the urgency to seek bribes, causing great harm to the people. He submitted a memorial: "From now on, when persons are requisitioned for military dispatch, offenders should provisionally be punished according to the law on receiving bribes during house-to-house assessments, so that petty men may have something to fear."
translations.idiomatic: When taxes and levies were raised for military needs, local officials did not always appoint trustworthy men; pursuing clerks and runners exploited the urgency of the work to extort bribes, to the people's deep injury. He proposed: "Henceforth, whenever men are conscripted for military dispatch, offenders should temporarily be punished under the statute on taking bribes during household assessments, so that petty officials may learn to fear the law."

sentences.zh: 二年六月，定制，因軍前差發受財者，一貫以下徒二年，以上徒三年，十貫處死，從汝礪之言也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year a regulation was enacted: those receiving bribes during front-line conscription—less than one string, two years' penal servitude; more, three years; ten strings, death—with Ruli's proposal followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year (1197) a statute was fixed: anyone taking bribes during front-line conscription received two years' penal servitude for less than one string of cash, three years for more, and death for ten strings or above—following Ruli's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 時遇奏事，台臣亦令回避，汝礪乃上言：「國家置諫臣以備侍從，蓋欲周知時政以參得失，非徒使排行就列而已。

translations.literal: At that time when presenting business, censorate officials were also ordered to withdraw; Ruli then submitted: "The state appoints remonstrating officials to attend upon the ruler, intending that they may thoroughly know current policy and participate in weighing gains and losses—not merely to stand in ranks and file past.
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported to the throne, censorate officers were likewise sent away. Ruli submitted: "The state appoints remonstrators to attend the ruler so they may know current affairs in full and help judge what succeeds or fails—not merely to stand in formation and march in and out.

sentences.zh: 故唐制，凡中書、門下及三品以上入閣，必遣諫官隨之，俾預聞政事，冀其有所開說。

translations.literal: Therefore under Tang institutions, whenever the Secretariat, Chancellery, and officials of third rank and above entered the privy council, remonstrating officials were always sent to accompany them, enabling them to hear policy in advance in hope they might offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, whenever Secretariat and Chancellery ministers and officials of third rank or higher entered the privy council, remonstrators were always sent along so they could hear deliberations beforehand and perhaps offer advice.

sentences.zh: 今省台以下，遇朝奏事則一切回避，與諸侍衛之臣旅進旅退。

translations.literal: Now those below the Secretariat and Censorate, when court business is presented, are all made to withdraw, advancing and retiring in groups like ordinary guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: Today, whenever the Secretariat and Censorate present business at court, their officers are all sent away and march in and out with the guard staff like any other attendants.

sentences.zh: 殿廷論事初莫得聞，及其已行，又不詳其始末，遂事而諫，斯亦難矣。

translations.literal: They initially hear nothing of deliberations in the hall; when matters are already enacted they still do not know the full course from start to finish—remonstrating after the fact is likewise difficult.
translations.idiomatic: They never hear debate in the hall at the outset; when a decision is already enacted they still lack the full story from beginning to end. To remonstrate only after the fact is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 顧諫職為何如哉？

translations.literal: What then becomes of the remonstrating office?
translations.idiomatic: What, then, is left of the remonstrator's role?

sentences.zh: 若曰非材，擇人可也，豈可置之言責而疏遠若此。

translations.literal: If one says they lack talent, others may be chosen; how can they be placed in a speaking office yet kept at such distance?
translations.idiomatic: If the men are unfit, choose better ones—but how can you assign them a speaking office and keep them this far removed?

sentences.zh: 乞自今以往，有司奏事諫官得以預聞，庶望少補。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on, when offices present business, remonstrating officials may hear in advance, in hope of some small improvement.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on remonstrators be allowed to hear in advance whenever offices report business, so the office may serve some small use.

sentences.zh: 且修注之職，掌記言動，俱當一體。」

translations.literal: Moreover the duty of recording and annotating, which keeps account of words and actions, should be treated as one with this."
translations.idiomatic: The historians who record words and deeds should be treated the same way."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「年前十月嘗舉行推排之法，尋以逾時而止，誠知聖上愛民之深也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Last year in the tenth month the method of household assessment was once carried out, but soon halted because the season had passed—I truly know how deeply Your Majesty loves the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Last year in the tenth month we tried the household-assessment method, then stopped because the season was late—I know how deeply Your Majesty cares for the people.

sentences.zh: 切聞周制，以歲時定民之眾寡，辨物之多少，入其數于小司徒，以施政教，以行征令，三年則天下大比，按為定法。

translations.literal: I have heard that under Zhou institutions, each year the people's numbers were fixed and goods distinguished in quantity; the figures were entered with the Minor Minister of Education to apply government and instruction and execute levies and orders; every three years a great comparison was made throughout the realm and established as fixed law.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that under Zhou institutions the state each year fixed the people's numbers and tallied their goods, reporting to the minor minister of education to govern and levy; every three years a great comparison was made empire-wide and fixed as law.

sentences.zh: 伏自大定四年通檢前後，迄今三十餘年，其間雖兩經推排，其浮財物力，惟憑一時小民之語以為增減，有司惟務速定，不復推究其實。

translations.literal: Since the comprehensive inspection before and after the fourth year of Dading, more than thirty years have passed; though assessments were twice conducted in between, movable property and goods were increased or decreased solely on momentary statements of common people; offices only sought quick settlement and no longer investigated the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Since the comprehensive inspection around the fourth year of Dading (1164), more than thirty years have passed. Although assessments were held twice in that span, movable wealth was adjusted only on whatever commoners said at the moment; officials rushed to finish and never verified the facts.

sentences.zh: 由是豪強有力者符同而倖免，貧弱寡援者抑屈而無訴。

translations.literal: Hence the powerful and strong colluded and escaped by luck, while the poor and weak with few supporters were suppressed and had no appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful colluded and escaped; the poor, with no one to plead for them, were crushed and had no recourse.

sentences.zh: 況近年以來，邊方屢有調發，貧戶益多。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years the frontier has repeatedly seen levies and dispatch; poor households have grown ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the frontiers have been levied again and again, and poor households have only multiplied.

sentences.zh: 如止循例推排，緣去歲條理已行，人所通知，恐新強之家預為請囑狡獪之人，冀望至時同辭推唱。

translations.literal: If we merely follow precedent in assessment, because last year's regulations have already been carried out and people informed, I fear newly powerful families will beforehand seek favor and cunning men hope that when the time comes they may all chant the same words in pushing assessment.
translations.idiomatic: If we merely repeat the usual assessment, everyone already knows last year's rules; newly rich families will lobby in advance and the cunning will hope to chant the same story when the time comes.

sentences.zh: 或虛作貧之，故以產業低價質典，及將財物徙置他所，權止營運。

translations.literal: Some will falsely pose as poor, deliberately pledging property at low prices or moving goods elsewhere and temporarily ceasing operations.
translations.idiomatic: Some will feign poverty, mortgaging property cheaply, moving goods elsewhere, or halting business for the moment.

sentences.zh: 如此奸弊百端，欲望物力均一，難矣。

translations.literal: With such fraud in a hundred forms, to desire equalization of goods and property is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: With fraud in every form, an even distribution of wealth is hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 欲革斯弊，莫若據實通檢，預令有司照勘大定四年條理，嚴立罪賞，截日立限，關防禁約。

translations.literal: To reform these abuses, nothing is better than a factual comprehensive inspection, beforehand ordering offices to examine against the regulations of the fourth year of Dading, strictly fixing penalties and rewards, setting deadlines by the day, and imposing guards and prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: To end these abuses, nothing beats a truthful comprehensive inspection: order offices in advance to apply the fourth-year-of-Dading regulations, fix strict penalties and rewards, set firm deadlines, and enforce tight controls.

sentences.zh: 其間有可以輕重者斟酌行之，去煩碎而就簡易，戒搔擾而事鎮靜，使富者不得以苟避，困者有望於少息，則賦稅易辦，人免不均之患矣。」

translations.literal: Where matters may be light or heavy, let discretion be applied; remove trivialities and adopt simplicity, guard against harassment and keep affairs calm, so the rich may not evade by chance and the distressed may hope for slight relief—then taxes will be easy to collect and people spared the affliction of inequality."
translations.idiomatic: Where rules allow discretion between lighter and heavier treatment, use it; cut red tape, keep the work simple, forbid harassment, and keep affairs calm, so the rich cannot dodge their share and the distressed may breathe a little—then taxes will be easier to collect and the people spared gross inequality."

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省俟邊事息行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to implement it when frontier affairs had quieted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Secretariat to carry it out once frontier troubles had subsided.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，上諭尚書省，遣官詣各路通檢民力，命戶部尚書賈執剛與汝礪先推排在都兩警巡院，令諸路所差官視以為法焉。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month the emperor instructed the Secretariat to send officials to each circuit for comprehensive inspection of the people's strength; he ordered Minister of Revenue Jia Zhigang and Ruli first to conduct assessment in the capital's two patrol districts, directing officials dispatched by the circuits to take this as their model.
translations.idiomatic: That October the emperor told the Secretariat to send officials to every circuit to inspect the people's capacity for taxation. He ordered Minister of Revenue Jia Zhigang and Ruli to run the first assessment in the capital's two patrol districts so circuit appointees could follow their example.

sentences.zh: 尋為同知大興府事。

translations.literal: Soon after he became Vice Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice administrator of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，為陝西東路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year he became Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year (1199) he became transport commissioner for Shaanxi East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年七月，改西京路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Taihe he was transferred to Transport Commissioner of Xijing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Taihe (1201) he was transferred to transport commissioner of Xijing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，為北京臨潢府路按察使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he became Surveillance Commissioner of the Northern Capital Linhuangfu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year (1202) he became surveillance commissioner for the Northern Capital Linhuangfu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，遷河北西路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he was moved to Transport Commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year (1204) he was moved to transport commissioner of Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一月，進中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was advanced to Chief Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was promoted to chief transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year (1206) he was appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時鈔法不能流轉，汝礪隨事上言，多所更定，民甚便之，語在《食貨志》。

translations.literal: At that time paper currency could not circulate; Ruli submitted proposals on each matter, many of which were revised, greatly benefiting the people—the account is in the Treatise on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: Paper money was not circulating; Ruli proposed reforms on each issue, many of which were adopted to the people's great benefit—the details appear in the Treatise on Food and Goods.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其議，敕尚書省曰：「內外百官所司不同，比應詔言事者不啻千數，俱不達各司利害，汗漫陳說，莫能詳盡。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his proposals and charged the Secretariat: "Officials within and outside have different duties; recently those responding to edicts to speak on affairs number no fewer than a thousand, yet none grasp the gains and losses of their respective offices, offering diffuse statements unable to be thorough.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his proposals and instructed the Secretariat: "Officials inside and outside the court have different duties. Lately more than a thousand have answered edicts to speak on affairs, yet none grasp their own office's interests; their statements are diffuse and never thorough.

sentences.zh: 近惟戶部尚書高汝礪，論本部數事，並切事情，皆已行之。

translations.literal: Recently only Minister of Revenue Gao Ruli, discussing several matters of his ministry, all hit the mark and have been implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Recently only Minister of Revenue Gao Ruli, discussing several matters within his ministry, hit the mark on each; all have been enacted.

sentences.zh: 其諭內外百司各究利害舉明，若可舉而不即申聞，以致上司舉行者，量制其罰。」

translations.literal: Instruct all offices within and outside to each investigate gains and losses and present them clearly; if something may be proposed yet is not immediately reported, causing superiors to propose it instead, fix punishment in proportion."
translations.idiomatic: Tell every office inside and outside the court to investigate its own interests and report clearly. If something ought to be proposed but is not reported at once, so that a superior must propose it instead, fix proportional punishment."

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年六月，宣宗南遷，次邯鄲，拜汝礪為參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Zhenyou, when Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital south and halted at Handan, Ruli was appointed Participant in Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Zhenyou (1214), when Xuanzong moved the court south and paused at Handan, Ruli was appointed participant in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 次湯陰，上聞汴京穀價騰踴，慮扈從人至則愈貴，問宰臣何以處之。

translations.literal: Halting at Tangyin, the emperor heard that grain prices in Bianjing were soaring and feared that when the entourage arrived they would rise further; he asked the chief ministers how to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: At Tangyin he heard grain prices in Bianjing were soaring and feared they would rise further when the entourage arrived; he asked his chief ministers what to do.

sentences.zh: 皆請命留守司約束，汝礪獨曰：「物價低昂，朝夕或異，然糴多糶少則貴。

translations.literal: All asked that the garrison command be ordered to restrain prices; Ruli alone said: "Commodity prices rise and fall and may differ morning and evening, yet when buying is much and selling little, prices are high.
translations.idiomatic: All urged ordering the garrison command to control prices. Ruli alone said: "Prices rise and fall from day to day, but when buyers are many and sellers few, grain must be dear.

sentences.zh: 蓋諸路之人輻湊河南，糴者既多，安得不貴？

translations.literal: People from all circuits have converged on Henan; with so many buyers, how could prices not be high?
translations.idiomatic: People from every circuit have poured into Henan; with so many buyers, how could grain stay cheap?

sentences.zh: 若禁止之，有物之家皆將閉而不出，商旅轉販亦不復入城，則糴者益急而貴益甚矣。

translations.literal: If we forbid it, households with goods will all shut up and not release them; merchants transporting goods will no longer enter the city—then buyers will be more urgent and prices higher still.
translations.idiomatic: If you forbid trade, households with grain will hoard it; merchants will stop bringing goods into the city; buyers will grow more desperate and prices will climb still higher.

sentences.zh: 事有難易，不可不知，今少而難得者穀也，多而易致者鈔也，自當先其所難，後其所易， 多方開誘，務使出粟更鈔，則谷價自平矣。」

translations.literal: Matters have what is difficult and what is easy—this cannot be ignored. Now grain is scarce and hard to obtain, paper notes plentiful and easy to acquire; we should first tackle the difficult, then the easy, opening many paths of inducement and striving to make grain come forth in exchange for notes—then grain prices will level themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Some tasks are hard and some easy—you must know the difference. Grain is scarce and hard to obtain; paper notes are plentiful and easy to get. Tackle the hard task first, the easy one second: open every channel of incentive and get grain exchanged for notes, and grain prices will settle on their own."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，朝廷議徙河北軍戶家屬于河南，留其軍守衛郡縣，汝礪言：「此事果行，但便於豪強家耳，貧戶豈能徙？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year the court debated moving the families of Hebei military households to Henan while leaving the soldiers to guard prefectures and counties. Ruli said: "If this is truly carried out, it will only benefit powerful families—how could poor households move?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year (1215) the court debated moving Hebei military households' families to Henan while the soldiers remained to guard local prefectures. Ruli said: "If this is carried out, only powerful families will benefit—how can poor households move?

sentences.zh: 且安土重遷，人之情也。

translations.literal: Moreover to be content in one's native soil and loathe moving is human nature.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, attachment to native soil is human nature.

sentences.zh: 今使盡赴河南，彼一旦去其田園，扶攜老幼，驅馳道路，流離失所，豈不可憐。

translations.literal: Now to make them all go to Henan—they would at once leave their fields and gardens, supporting old and young, driven along the roads, displaced and homeless—is this not pitiable?
translations.idiomatic: To send them all to Henan at once is to tear them from their fields, drag old and young along the roads, and leave them homeless—is that not pitiable?

sentences.zh: 且所過百姓見軍戶盡遷，必將驚疑，謂國家分別彼此，其心安得不搖。

translations.literal: Moreover common people along the route, seeing military households all moved, will surely be alarmed and suspicious, thinking the state distinguishes us from them—how could their hearts not be shaken?
translations.idiomatic: Commoners along the route, seeing every military household uprooted, will be alarmed and suspect the state favors one group over another—how could their hearts stay steady?

sentences.zh: 況軍人已去其家，而令護衛他人，以情度之，其不肯盡心必矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the soldiers have already lost their families yet are ordered to guard others' homes—judging by feeling, they will surely not devote their full hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers have lost their own families yet must guard others' homes—by ordinary feeling they surely will not give their full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 民至愚而神者也，雖告以衛護之意，亦將不信，徒令交亂，俱不得安，此其利害所系至重。

translations.literal: The people are most foolish yet also most sensitive; even if told the intent is protection, they will not believe—only causing mutual disorder so none may be at peace. The gains and losses involved are weighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The people are simple yet uncannily perceptive: even told the move is for their protection, they will not believe it. You will only breed disorder and leave no one secure. The stakes are very high.

sentences.zh: 乞先令諸道元帥府、宣撫司、總管府熟論可否，如無可疑，然後施行。」

translations.literal: I beg that the marshal's offices, pacification commissions, and chief command offices of each circuit first thoroughly debate whether it is feasible; if nothing is doubtful, then implement."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each circuit's marshal's office, pacification commission, and chief command first debate the plan thoroughly; if no doubt remains, then enact it."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: He received no answer.

sentences.zh: 軍戶既遷，將括地分授之，未有定論，上敕尚書省曰：「北兵將及河南，由是盡起諸路軍戶，共圖保守。

translations.literal: After the military households had moved, land was to be surveyed and apportioned to them, but no decision had been fixed. The emperor charged the Secretariat: "Northern troops are about to reach Henan; therefore all military households of the circuits were raised to plan defense together.
translations.idiomatic: After the military households had moved, the court planned to survey land and allot it to them, but no decision was fixed. The emperor instructed the Secretariat: "Northern armies are nearing Henan, so we have called up military households from every circuit to help defend the region.

sentences.zh: 今既至矣，糧食所當必與，然未有以處之。

translations.literal: Now they have arrived; grain must certainly be provided, yet there is as yet no means to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: They have arrived, and grain must be supplied, but we still have no settled plan.

sentences.zh: 可分遣官聚耆老問之，其將益賦，或與之田，二者孰便。」

translations.literal: Officials may be dispatched separately to gather elders and ask whether they prefer increased levies or being given land—which of the two is more convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Send officials to gather local elders and ask whether they prefer higher levies or allotting land to the soldiers—which is better."

sentences.zh: 又以諭汝礪。

translations.literal: This was also communicated to Ruli.
translations.idiomatic: The same instruction was relayed to Ruli.

sentences.zh: 既而所遣官言：「農民並稱，比年以來，租賦已重，若更益之，力實不足，不敢複佃官田，願以給軍。」

translations.literal: Soon the dispatched officials reported: "Peasants all said that in recent years rents and levies have already been heavy; if increased further their strength is truly insufficient—they dare not again tenant state land and wish to give it to the army."
translations.idiomatic: The officials soon reported: "The peasants all said rents and levies have already been heavy in recent years; they cannot bear more and dare not keep leasing state land—they wish to give it to the army."

sentences.zh: 於是汝礪奏：「遷徙軍戶，一時之事也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ruli memorialized: "Moving military households is a matter of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli then memorialized: "Moving military households is a temporary measure.

sentences.zh: 民佃官田，久遠之計也。

translations.literal: Peasants tenanting state land is a plan for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants leasing state land is a long-term arrangement.

sentences.zh: 河南民地、官田，計數相半。

translations.literal: In Henan private land and state land are roughly equal in count.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan private land and state land are roughly equal in extent.

sentences.zh: 又多全佃官田之家，墳塋、莊井俱在其中。

translations.literal: Many households lease state land entirely, with ancestral graves and farmstead wells all within it.
translations.idiomatic: Many households lease state land exclusively, with ancestral graves and farmstead wells on the same plots.

sentences.zh: 率皆貧民，一旦奪之，何以自活？

translations.literal: They are mostly poor people—if seized at once, how may they support themselves?
translations.idiomatic: They are mostly poor; if you seize the land at once, how will they live?

sentences.zh: 夫小民易動難安，一時避賦，遂有此言。

translations.literal: Common people are easily stirred and hard to settle; for a moment avoiding levies they therefore spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners are easily stirred and hard to reassure; for the moment they spoke thus to avoid heavier levies.

sentences.zh: 及其與人，即前日之主，今還為客，能勿悔乎？

translations.literal: When they have given it to others, they who were masters yesterday become guests today—can they not regret?
translations.idiomatic: Once they have given the land away, yesterday's masters become today's tenants—will they not regret it?

sentences.zh: 悔則忿心生矣。

translations.literal: With regret, resentment is born.
translations.idiomatic: Regret will breed resentment.

sentences.zh: 如山東撥地時，腴田沃壤盡入勢家，瘠惡者乃付貧戶。

translations.literal: As when land was allotted in Shandong, fertile fields and rich soil all went to powerful families while poor and bad land was given to poor households.
translations.idiomatic: When land was allotted in Shandong, fertile fields went entirely to powerful families while poor soil was handed to poor households.

sentences.zh: 無益於軍，而民則有損，至於互相憎疾，今猶未已，前事不遠，足為明戒。

translations.literal: It did not benefit the army yet harmed the people, even to mutual hatred that has not ceased even now—the recent past is not far and suffices as a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: The army gained nothing while the people suffered; mutual hatred from that time has not ended. The recent past is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 惟當倍益官租，以給軍糧之半，複以系官荒田、牧馬草地量數付之，令其自耕，則百姓免失業之艱，而官司不必為厲民之事矣。

translations.literal: We should only double state rents to supply half the army's grain, and also allot in measured amount state wasteland and horse pasture that may be cultivated, letting them farm for themselves—then the people are spared the hardship of losing livelihood and the government need not do what harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: Only double the rent on state land to supply half the army's grain, and allot measured tracts of state wasteland and pasture for them to farm themselves. The people will avoid losing their livelihood, and the government need not harm them.

sentences.zh: 且河南之田最宜麥，今雨澤沾足，正播種之時，誠恐民疑以誤歲計，宜早決之。」

translations.literal: Moreover Henan's fields are best suited to wheat; now rain and moisture are ample and it is precisely sowing time—I truly fear the people will be suspicious and miss the year's plan; it should be decided early."
translations.idiomatic: Henan's fields suit wheat best; rain is ample and sowing season is here. I fear popular suspicion will ruin the year's harvest if we delay—decide quickly."

sentences.zh: 上從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時上以軍戶地當撥付，使得及時耕墾，而汝礪複上奏曰：「在官荒田及牧馬地，民多私耕者。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor held that military household land should be allotted so they could plow in season; Ruli again memorialized: "On state wasteland and horse pasture the people mostly farm in private.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted military households to receive land in time for planting. Ruli memorialized again: "Much state wasteland and pasture is already being farmed privately.

sentences.zh: 今正藝麥之時，彼知將以與人，必皆棄去。

translations.literal: Now it is precisely the season for planting wheat; knowing it will be given to others, they will surely all abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: It is wheat-planting season; once they know the land will be taken away, they will abandon their crops.

sentences.zh: 軍戶雖得，亦已逾時，徒成曠廢。

translations.literal: Even if military households receive it, the season will have passed—only creating waste and desolation.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the military households receive the land, the season will be past and the fields will lie waste.

sentences.zh: 若候畢功而後撥，量收所得，以補軍儲，則公私俱便。

translations.literal: If we wait until the harvest is finished before allotting, take a measured share of the yield to supplement army stores—then public and private interests are both served.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until the harvest, take a measured share for army stores, and then allot the land, both state and people benefit.

sentences.zh: 乞盡九月然後遣官。」

translations.literal: I beg to send officials only after the ninth month is complete."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that officials be sent only after the ninth month."

sentences.zh: 十月，汝礪言：「今河北軍戶徙河南者幾百萬口，人日給米一升，歲率三百六十萬石，半給其直猶支粟三百萬石。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Ruli said: "Now Hebei military households moved to Henan number nearly several million persons; each person is given one sheng of rice daily, yearly totaling 3,600,000 shi—even giving half in cash still requires 3,000,000 shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Ruli said: "Nearly several million mouths of Hebei military households have moved to Henan. At one sheng of rice per person per day, the yearly total is 3,600,000 shi; even paying half in cash still requires 3,000,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 河南租地計二十四萬頃，歲征粟才一百五十六萬有奇，更乞於經費之外倍征以給，仍以系官閒田及牧馬地可耕者畀之。」

translations.literal: Henan's leased land totals 240,000 qing; yearly grain levied is only a little over 1,560,000—I further beg that beyond regular expenses it be doubled for supply, and that state idle land and cultivable horse pasture still be allotted."
translations.idiomatic: Henan's leased land totals 240,000 qing and yields only a little over 1,560,000 shi yearly. I ask that rents be doubled beyond ordinary expenses for this supply, and that state idle land and cultivable pasture still be allotted."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 乃遣右司諫馮開等分詣諸郡就給之，人三十畝，以汝礪總之。

translations.literal: Right Bureau Remonstrator Feng Kai and others were then dispatched separately to each prefecture to grant on the spot thirty mu per person, with Ruli overseeing the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Right bureau remonstrator Feng Kai and others were sent to each prefecture to grant thirty mu per person on the spot, with Ruli in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 既而括地官還，皆曰：「頃畝之數甚少，且瘠惡不可耕。

translations.literal: When the land-survey officials returned, all said: "The number of mu is very small and moreover poor and bad, unable to be cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: When the land-survey officials returned, they all said: "The acreage is very small and the soil too poor to farm.

sentences.zh: 計其可耕者均以與之，人得無幾，又僻遠處不免徙就之，軍人皆以為不便。」

translations.literal: Calculating what is cultivable and dividing it equally among them, each person receives almost nothing; moreover in remote places they cannot avoid moving to take it—the soldiers all find it inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: Even dividing all cultivable land equally, each man receives almost nothing; in remote districts they must move to claim it. The soldiers all find the arrangement unworkable."

sentences.zh: 汝礪遂言於上，詔有司罷之，但給軍糧之半，而半折以實直焉。

translations.literal: Ruli then spoke to the emperor; an edict ordered the offices to halt it, only giving half the army grain while the other half was converted to actual cash value.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli reported to the emperor; an edict halted the land grant. Only half the grain ration was kept; the other half was paid in cash at full value.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，拜尚書左丞，連上表乞致仕，皆優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat; he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement, all met with gracious edicts refusing permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (1216) he was appointed left vice minister of the Secretariat. He repeatedly asked to retire; each time the throne graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷議發兵河北，護民芟麥，而民間流言謂官將盡取之。

translations.literal: Just then the court debated dispatching troops to Hebei to protect the people in harvesting wheat, while popular rumor said officials would take it all.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court debated sending troops to Hebei to protect the harvest, while rumor spread that officials would seize all the grain.

sentences.zh: 上聞，以問宰職曰：「為之奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and asked the chief officials: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and asked his chief ministers: "What should we do?"

sentences.zh: 高琪等奏：「若令樞密院遣兵居其沖要，鎮遏土寇，仍許收逃戶之田，則軍民兩便。

translations.literal: Gao Qi and others memorialized: "If the Bureau of Military Affairs is ordered to send troops to hold key points and suppress local bandits, still permitting them to take fields of fugitive households, then army and people are both served.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi and others proposed: "Let the Bureau of Military Affairs post troops at key points to suppress local bandits and allow them to take fugitives' fields—both army and people will benefit.

sentences.zh: 或有警急，軍士亦必盡心。」

translations.literal: If there is urgent alarm, the soldiers will also surely give their full hearts."
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency the soldiers will surely fight with full loyalty."

sentences.zh: 汝礪曰：「甚非計也。

translations.literal: Ruli said: "This is a very poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli said: "That is a very poor plan.

sentences.zh: 蓋河朔之民所恃以食者，惟此麥耳。

translations.literal: The people of the Yellow River north rely for food on this wheat alone.
translations.idiomatic: The people north of the Yellow River depend on this wheat alone for food.

sentences.zh: 今已有流言，而複以兵往，是益使之疑懼也。

translations.literal: Now there is already rumor, and to send troops again is only to increase their suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor already circulates; sending troops will only deepen their fear.

sentences.zh: 不若聽其自便，令宣撫司禁戢無賴，不致侵擾足矣。

translations.literal: Better to let them manage for themselves and order the Pacification Commission to restrain ruffians so they do not harass—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Better let them manage on their own and order the pacification commission to restrain ruffians from harassment—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 逃戶田令有司收之，以充軍儲可也。」

translations.literal: Let offices take fields of fugitive households to fill army stores—that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Let offices take fugitives' fields for army stores—that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 乃詔遣戶部員外郎裴滿蒲剌都閱視田數，及訪民願發兵以否，還奏：「臣西由懷、孟，東抵曹、單，麥苗苦亦無多，訊諸農民，往往自為義軍。

translations.literal: An edict then dispatched Revenue Bureau Vice Director Peiman Puladu to inspect field counts and inquire whether the people wished troops sent; returning he memorialized: "Your servant went west from Huai and Meng, east to Cao and Shan—the wheat seedlings are bitter and not plentiful; questioning the peasants, many have already formed righteous armies themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Revenue Bureau vice director Peiman Puladu to inspect the fields and ask whether the people wanted troops. On his return he reported: "I traveled west from Huai and Meng to Cao and Shan—the wheat crop is poor and sparse. Many peasants have already formed local militias on their own.

sentences.zh: 臣即宣佈朝廷欲發兵之意，皆感戴而不願也。」

translations.literal: Your servant then announced the court's intent to send troops; all were grateful yet unwilling."
translations.idiomatic: I then announced the court's plan to send troops; all expressed gratitude but none wished it."

sentences.zh: 於是罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 汝礪以數乞致仕不從，乃上言曰：「立非常之功，必待非常之人。

translations.literal: Ruli, having repeatedly begged to retire without success, then submitted: "To establish extraordinary achievement, one must await extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli had repeatedly asked to retire without success. He then submitted: "Extraordinary achievements require extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 今大兵既退，正完葺關隘、簡練兵士之時，須得通敏經綸之才預為籌畫，俾濟中興。

translations.literal: Now that the great armies have withdrawn, it is precisely the time to complete border passes and drill soldiers; we need penetrating and versatile talents in statecraft to plan in advance and thereby aid restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The great armies have withdrawn; now is the time to repair the passes and train the troops. We need penetrating minds in statecraft to plan ahead and help restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 伏見尚書左丞兼行樞密副使胥鼎，才擅眾長，身兼數器，乞召還朝省。」

translations.literal: I humbly observe Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Acting Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Xu Ding, whose talent excels in many fields and who personally combines many capacities—I beg that he be summoned back to the central government."
translations.idiomatic: I observe Left Vice Minister Xu Ding, also acting vice commissioner of military affairs, whose talent spans many fields. I beg that he be recalled to the central government."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時高琪欲從言事者歲閱民田征租，朝廷將從之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Qi wished to follow memorialists in yearly inspection of civilian fields for tax collection; the court was about to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi wished to follow memorialists who proposed yearly inspection of civilian fields for tax collection; the court was about to agree.

sentences.zh: 汝礪言：「臣聞治大國者若烹小鮮，最為政之善喻也。

translations.literal: Ruli said: "I have heard that governing a great state is like cooking a small fish—the finest analogy for government.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli said: "I have heard that governing a great state is like cooking a small fish—the finest analogy for good government.

sentences.zh: 國朝自大定通檢後，十年一推物力，惟其貴簡靜而重勞民耳。

translations.literal: Our dynasty, since the comprehensive inspection of Dading, assesses property every ten years, valuing simplicity and quiet and dreading to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Dading comprehensive inspection, our dynasty has assessed property every ten years, valuing simplicity and dreading to burden the people.

sentences.zh: 今言者請如河北歲括實種之田，計數征斂，即是常時通檢，無乃駭人視聽，使之不安乎。

translations.literal: Now the memorialists ask, as in Hebei, yearly to survey fields actually planted and levy by count—this is constant comprehensive inspection; will it not alarm eyes and ears and make people uneasy?
translations.idiomatic: The memorialists now ask to survey actually planted fields yearly as in Hebei and levy by count—that is constant comprehensive inspection. Will it not alarm the people and unsettle them?

sentences.zh: 且河南、河北事體不同。

translations.literal: Moreover the circumstances of Henan and Hebei differ.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Henan and Hebei are not the same case.

sentences.zh: 河北累經劫掠，戶口亡匿，田疇荒廢，差調難依元額，故為此權宜之法，蓋軍儲不加多，且地少而易見也。

translations.literal: Hebei has repeatedly suffered plunder; households have fled and hidden, fields lie waste, and levies cannot follow the original quotas—hence this expedient method, for army stores would not greatly increase and moreover the land is little and easy to survey.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei has been repeatedly plundered; people have fled and fields lie waste, so levies cannot follow old quotas. Hence the expedient method: army stores would not greatly increase, and the land is sparse and easy to survey.

sentences.zh: 河南自車駕巡幸以來，百姓湊集，凡有閒田及逃戶所棄，耕墾殆遍，各承元戶輸租，其所征斂，皆准通推之額，雖軍馬益多，未嘗闕誤，詎宜一概動擾。

translations.literal: Since the imperial carriage toured Henan, the people have gathered; wherever there was idle land or what fugitive households abandoned, cultivation is nearly complete; each continues the original household's rent payments, and collections all follow the comprehensive assessment quota—even as troops and horses increase, there has never been shortfall; how can we uniformly stir disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor toured Henan, people have gathered and cultivated nearly every idle plot and abandoned field. Each pays rent under the original household quota at comprehensive-assessment rates. Though troops have increased, collections have never fallen short. Why stir everyone up uniformly?

sentences.zh: 若恐豪右蔽匿而逋征賦，則有司檢括亦豈盡實。

translations.literal: If one fears powerful families conceal and evade taxes, can official inspection be fully truthful either?
translations.idiomatic: If you fear powerful families hide wealth and evade taxes, official inspection will not be fully truthful either.

sentences.zh: 但嚴立賞罰，許其自首，及聽人告捕，犯者以盜軍儲坐之，地付告者，自足使人知懼，而賦悉入官，何必為是紛紛也。

translations.literal: Only strictly fix rewards and penalties, permit self-report, and allow others to denounce and arrest; offenders are punished as stealing army stores, land given to the accuser—this alone suffices to make people fear, and all taxes enter the state. Why must we be so tumultuous?
translations.idiomatic: Only fix strict rewards and penalties, allow self-report, and permit denunciation. Punish offenders as thieves of army stores and give the land to accusers—that alone will make people fear, and all taxes will reach the treasury. Why create such turmoil?

sentences.zh: 抑又有大不可者三：如每歲檢括，則夏田春量，秋田夏量，中間雜種亦且隨時量之，一歲中略無休息，民將厭避，耕種失時，或止耕膏腴而棄其餘，則所收仍舊而所輸益少，一不可也。

translations.literal: Moreover there are three great impossibilities: if yearly inspection, summer fields are measured in spring, autumn fields in summer, and mixed crops in season too—through the year there is scarcely rest; the people will grow weary and avoid it, planting will miss its season, or they will only farm fertile soil and abandon the rest—then harvest stays the same while payments grow less. First impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: There are three grave objections. Yearly inspection means measuring summer fields in spring and autumn fields in summer, with mixed crops measured in season too—the people have no rest all year, will grow weary, and miss planting seasons; some will farm only fertile soil and abandon the rest, so harvest stays the same while tax yield falls. First objection.

sentences.zh: 檢括之時，縣官不能家至戶到，裏胥得以暗通貨賂，上下其手，虛為文具，轉失其真，二不可也。

translations.literal: At inspection time county officials cannot visit every household; village clerks may secretly take bribes and manipulate records, making empty documents and losing the truth—second impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: At inspection time county officials cannot visit every household; village clerks will take bribes and falsify records. Second objection.

sentences.zh: 民田與軍田犬牙相錯，彼或陰結軍人以相冒亂，而朝廷止憑有司之籍，倘使臨時少於元額，則資儲闕誤必矣，三不可也。

translations.literal: Civilian and military fields interlock like dog teeth; they may secretly collude with soldiers to confuse boundaries while the court relies only on official registers—if at the moment the amount falls short of the original quota, stores will surely fail—third impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian and military fields interlock; locals may collude with soldiers to confuse boundaries while the court relies only on registers. If collections fall below the original quota, army stores will surely fail. Third objection.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷舉事，務在必行，既行而複中止焉，是豈善計哉。」

translations.literal: When the court undertakes affairs it strives for certain execution; to execute and then halt again—is this a good plan?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court undertakes a policy it must see it through; to enact and then halt—is that sound policy?"

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The debate was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 興定元年十月，上疏曰：「言者請姑與宋人議和以息邊民，切以為非計。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Xingding he submitted a memorial: "Memorialists ask to discuss peace with the Song for the moment to give border people rest—I deem this no plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Xingding (1217) he memorialized: "Memorialists ask to discuss peace with the Song for the moment to ease border suffering. I deem this unwise.

sentences.zh: 宋人多詐無實，雖與文移往來，而邊備未敢遽撤。

translations.literal: The Song are mostly deceitful and insubstantial; even if documents are exchanged, border defenses dare not be hastily withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Song are deceitful; even if documents are exchanged, we dare not hastily withdraw border defenses.

sentences.zh: 備既不撤，則議和與否蓋無以異。

translations.literal: If defenses are not withdrawn, then whether peace is discussed or not is essentially no different.
translations.idiomatic: If defenses stay in place, discussing peace or not makes little difference.

sentences.zh: 或複蔓以浮辭，禮例之外別有求索，言涉不遜，將若之何？

translations.literal: Or they may again spin empty words, seeking beyond ritual precedent—if their language is insubordinate, what then?
translations.idiomatic: They may spin empty words and demand beyond ritual precedent. If their language is insubordinate, what then?

sentences.zh: 或曰：'大定間亦嘗先遣使，今何不可？

translations.literal: Some say: 'In Dading we also once sent envoys first—why not now?'
translations.idiomatic: Some say: 'In the Dading era we also sent envoys first—why not now?'

sentences.zh: '切謂時殊事異，難以例言。

translations.literal: I deem the times and affairs differ and precedent cannot apply.
translations.idiomatic: I deem the times and circumstances differ; precedent cannot apply.

sentences.zh: 昔海陵師出無名，曲在於我，是以世宗即位，首遣高忠建等報諭宋主，罷淮甸所侵以修舊好。

translations.literal: Formerly Hailing marched without just cause—the fault was ours; therefore when Shizong took the throne he first sent Gao Zhongjian and others to inform the Song ruler, ceasing Huai region encroachments to restore the old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Hailing marched without just cause—the fault was ours. When Shizong took the throne he first sent Gao Zhongjian and others to inform the Song ruler and cease Huai encroachments to restore friendship.

sentences.zh: 彼隨遣使來，書辭慢易，不復奉表稱臣，願還故疆，為兄弟國。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys in return; their letters were disrespectful, no longer submitting memorials as subjects, wishing to recover old territory and become brother states.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys in return with disrespectful letters, no longer submitting memorials as subjects, wishing to recover old territory and become brother states.

sentences.zh: 雖其樞密院與我帥府時通書問，而侵軼未嘗已也。

translations.literal: Although their Bureau of Military Affairs and our command offices sometimes exchanged letters, encroachments never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Although their Bureau of Military Affairs and our command offices sometimes exchanged letters, border raids never ceased.

sentences.zh: 既而征西元帥合喜敗宋將吳璘、姚良輔於德順、原州，右丞相僕散忠義、右副元帥紇石烈志甯敗李世輔於宿州，斬首五萬，兵威大振。

translations.literal: Soon after, Western Campaign Marshal He Xi defeated Song generals Wu Lin and Yao Liangfu at Shun and Yuan Prefectures; Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi and Right Vice Marshal Heseli Zhinning defeated Li Shipu at Suzhou, beheading fifty thousand—the army's prestige greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Western Campaign Marshal He Xi defeated Song generals Wu Lin and Yao Liangfu at Shun and Yuan; Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi and Right Vice Marshal Heseli Zhinning defeated Li Shipu at Suzhou, beheading fifty thousand—the army's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂宰臣曰：'昔宋人，言遣使請和，乘吾無備遂攻宿州，今為我軍大敗，殺戮過當，故不敢複通問。

translations.literal: Shizong told the chief ministers: 'Formerly the Song, claiming to send envoys to sue for peace, attacked Suzhou when we were unprepared; now our army has greatly defeated them and slaughtered excessively—they dare not communicate again.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told the chief ministers: 'Formerly the Song claimed to send envoys for peace, then attacked Suzhou when we were unprepared. Now our army has crushed them with excessive slaughter—they dare not communicate again.

sentences.zh: 朕哀南北生靈久困於兵，本欲息民，何較細故，其令帥府移書宋人，以議和好。

translations.literal: I pity the people north and south long afflicted by war and originally wished to give the people rest—why quibble over trifles? Order the command office to send letters to the Song to discuss peace.'
translations.idiomatic: I pity the people north and south long afflicted by war and wish to give them rest—why quibble over trifles? Order the command office to write the Song to discuss peace.'

sentences.zh: '宋果遣使告和，以當時堂堂之勢，又無邊患，竟免其奉表稱臣之禮。

translations.literal: The Song indeed sent envoys suing for peace; with our imposing strength at the time and no border troubles, they were finally spared the ritual of submitting memorials as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent envoys suing for peace. With our imposing strength and no border troubles, they were finally spared submitting memorials as subjects.

sentences.zh: 今宋棄信背盟，侵我邊鄙，是曲在彼也。

translations.literal: Now the Song have abandoned faith and broken the alliance, encroaching on our borders—the fault is theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Song have broken faith and encroached on our borders—the fault is theirs.

sentences.zh: 彼若請和，於理為順，豈當先發此議而自示弱耶？

translations.literal: If they sue for peace, that accords with reason; how should we initiate this proposal and show weakness ourselves?
translations.idiomatic: If they sue for peace, that is reasonable; why should we initiate the proposal and show weakness?

sentences.zh: 恐非徒無益，反招謗侮而已。」

translations.literal: I fear it will not merely be useless but invite slander and contempt."
translations.idiomatic: I fear it will not merely fail but invite contempt."

sentences.zh: 十一月，汝礪言：「臣聞國以民為基，民以財為本，是以王者必先愛養基本。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Ruli said: "I have heard that the state takes the people as foundation and the people take wealth as root; therefore the king must first cherish and nurture the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Ruli said: "I have heard that the state rests on the people and the people rest on wealth; therefore a ruler must first cherish and nurture that foundation.

sentences.zh: 國家調發，河南為重，所徵稅租率常三倍於舊。

translations.literal: In state levies Henan bears the heaviest burden; taxes and rents collected are routinely triple the old amount.
translations.idiomatic: In state levies Henan bears the heaviest burden; taxes and rents collected are routinely triple the old amount.

sentences.zh: 今省部計歲收通寶不敷所支，乃於民間科斂桑皮故紙錢七千萬貫以補之。

translations.literal: Now the ministries calculate yearly Tongbao receipts insufficient for expenditures and therefore levy on the people seventy million strings in mulberry-bark and waste-paper money to supplement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries find yearly Tongbao receipts insufficient for expenditures and have levied seventy million strings in mulberry-bark and waste-paper money from the people to make up the gap.

sentences.zh: 近以通寶稍滯，又加兩倍。

translations.literal: Recently because Tongbao circulation has slowed, it was doubled again.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because Tongbao circulation has slowed, the levy was doubled again.

sentences.zh: 河南人戶，農民居三之二，今稅租猶多未足，而此令複出，彼不糶所當輸租，則必減其食以應之。

translations.literal: Of Henan households, farmers are two-thirds; now many rents are still unpaid, yet this order appears again—if they do not sell grain for rent due, they must reduce their food to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thirds of Henan households are farmers. Many still cannot pay their rents, yet this order appears again. If they do not sell grain to pay rent, they must cut their food to meet the levy.

sentences.zh: 夫事有難易，勢有緩急。

translations.literal: Matters have what is difficult and easy; situations have what is urgent and slack.
translations.idiomatic: Some tasks are hard and some easy; some situations urgent and some not.

sentences.zh: 今急用而難得者，芻糧也，出於民力，其來有限，可緩圖。

translations.literal: What is urgently needed yet hard to obtain is fodder and grain, coming from the people's strength in limited supply—it may be planned slowly.
translations.idiomatic: What is urgently needed yet hard to obtain is fodder and grain, which comes from limited popular labor and can be planned gradually.

sentences.zh: 而易為者，鈔法也，行於國家，其變無窮。

translations.literal: What is easy is paper currency, circulating through the state with endless transformations.
translations.idiomatic: What is easy is paper currency, which the state can transform endlessly.

sentences.zh: 向者大鈔滯，更為小鈔，小鈔弊，改為寶券，寶券不行，易為通寶，從權制變，皆由於上，尚何以煩民為哉。

translations.literal: Formerly large notes stagnated and were changed to small notes; small notes failed and were changed to treasure certificates; certificates would not circulate and were changed to Tongbao—all expedient changes from above—why still trouble the people?
translations.idiomatic: Large notes stagnated and became small notes; small notes failed and became treasure certificates; certificates failed and became Tongbao—all expedient changes from above. Why still trouble the people?

sentences.zh: 彼悉力以奉軍儲已患不足，而又添征通寶，苟不能給，則有逃亡。

translations.literal: They already strain to supply army stores and find it insufficient; adding Tongbao levies, if they cannot pay, there will be flight.
translations.idiomatic: They already strain to supply army stores and fall short; if they cannot pay added Tongbao levies, they will flee.

sentences.zh: 民逃亡則農事廢，兵食何自而得？

translations.literal: If the people flee, farming is abandoned—whence will army food come?
translations.idiomatic: If the people flee, farming collapses—whence will army food come?

sentences.zh: 有司不究遠圖而貪近效，不固本原而較末節，誠恐軍儲、鈔法兩有所妨。

translations.literal: Offices do not investigate long-term plans but covet near results, do not consolidate the root but compare minor ends—I truly fear both army stores and currency will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Offices covet quick results instead of long-term plans and tweak minor ends instead of securing the root. I fear both army stores and currency policy will suffer.

sentences.zh: 臣非於鈔法不為意也，非於省部故相違也，但以鈔法稍滯物價稍增之害輕，民生不安軍儲不給之害重耳。

translations.literal: Your servant is not unconcerned with currency nor deliberately opposing the ministries—but sluggish currency and slightly rising prices are light harm, while popular unrest and failed army stores are heavy harm.
translations.idiomatic: I am not unconcerned with currency nor deliberately opposing the ministries—but sluggish currency and slightly rising prices are lesser harms; popular unrest and failed army stores are the greater.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下外度事勢，俯察臣言，特命有司減免，則群心和悅，而未足之租有所望矣。」

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty outwardly gauges the situation and inwardly examines my words, specially ordering offices to reduce and remit, will the multitude be harmonious and unpaid rents have hope."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty gauges the situation and heeds my words, ordering offices to reduce and remit levies, the people will be reassured and unpaid rents may yet be collected."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以賈仝、苗道潤等相攻不和，將分畀州縣、別署名號以處之。

translations.literal: At that time because Jia Tong, Miao Daorun, and others attacked each other without harmony, the court planned to divide prefectures and counties among them and assign separate titles to settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jia Tong, Miao Daorun, and others were fighting each other, the court planned to divide prefectures and counties among them under separate titles.

sentences.zh: 汝礪上書曰：「甚非計也。

translations.literal: Ruli submitted a letter: "This is a very poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli submitted: "This is a very poor plan.

sentences.zh: 蓋河北諸帥多本土義軍，一時權為隊長，亦有先嘗叛亡者，非若素宦於朝，知禮義、識名分之人也。

translations.literal: The commanders of Hebei are mostly local righteous-army men who for a time served as squad leaders; some had previously rebelled and fled—they are not like those long in court service who know ritual and propriety and understand ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei commanders are mostly local militia leaders who rose as squad chiefs; some had previously rebelled. They are not long-serving court officials who know ritual and ranks.

sentences.zh: 貪暴不法，蓋無足怪。

translations.literal: Greedy, violent, and lawless—they are hardly to be wondered at.
translations.idiomatic: Their greed, violence, and lawlessness are hardly surprising.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以時方多故，姑牢籠用之，庶使遣民少得安息。

translations.literal: The court, because troubles were many, temporarily kept them in harness for use, hoping displaced people might gain a little rest.
translations.idiomatic: The court, with troubles everywhere, temporarily kept them in harness so displaced people might gain a little rest.

sentences.zh: 彼互相攻劫則勢浸弱，勢力既弱則朝廷易制。

translations.literal: If they attack and plunder each other their power gradually weakens; once weakened the court easily controls them.
translations.idiomatic: If they attack each other their power weakens; once weakened the court can control them easily.

sentences.zh: 今若分地而與之，州縣官吏得輒署置，民戶稅賦得擅徵收，則地廣者日益強，狹者日益弱。

translations.literal: Now if land is divided and given them, with prefectural officials freely appointing and household taxes freely collected, those with broad territory grow daily stronger and the narrow daily weaker.
translations.idiomatic: If you divide land among them and let them appoint officials and collect taxes freely, the strong grow stronger and the weak weaker.

sentences.zh: 久之，弱者皆並于強，強者之地不可複奪，是朝廷愈難制也。

translations.literal: In time the weak are all absorbed by the strong; the strong's territory cannot be retaken—the court grows harder to control.
translations.idiomatic: In time the weak will be absorbed by the strong, whose territory cannot be retaken—the court will be harder to control.

sentences.zh: 昔唐分河朔地授諸叛將，史臣謂其護養孽萌以成其禍，此可為今日大戒也。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang divided Hebei land among rebel generals; historians said they nurtured evil sprouts to complete their disaster—this should be today's great warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang divided Hebei among rebel generals, historians said they nurtured evil sprouts to their ruin—that is today's great warning.

sentences.zh: 不若姑令行省羈縻和輯，多方牽制，使之不得逞。

translations.literal: Better temporarily to let the Branch Secretariat restrain and reconcile them, checking them in many ways so they cannot act freely.
translations.idiomatic: Better let the Branch Secretariat restrain and reconcile them, checking them in many ways so they cannot act freely.

sentences.zh: 異時邊事稍息，氣力漸完，若輩又何足患哉。」

translations.literal: When border affairs later quiet and strength gradually recovers, what worry are such men?"
translations.idiomatic: When border affairs quiet and strength recovers, what worry are such men?"

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The debate was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂汝礪曰：「朕每見卿侍朝，恐不任其勞，許坐殿下，而卿終不從何哉？

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Ruli: "Each time I see you attending court I fear you cannot bear the labor and permit you to sit below the hall—yet you never comply. Why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Ruli: "Each time I see you at court I fear the strain is too much and permit you to sit below the hall—yet you never accept. Why?

sentences.zh: 夫君臣相遇，貴在誠實，小謹區區，朕固不較也。」

translations.literal: When ruler and minister meet, sincerity is prized; petty caution in trifles—I truly do not mind."
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister meet, sincerity matters most; I do not mind petty formalities."

sentences.zh: 汝礪以君臣之分甚嚴，不敢奉命。

translations.literal: Ruli, holding the distinction between ruler and minister very strict, did not dare obey.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli held the distinction between ruler and minister too strict to obey.

sentences.zh: 三年，河南頗豐稔，民間多積粟，汝礪乃奏曰：「國家之務，莫重於食，今所在屯兵益眾，而修築新城其費亦廣，若不及此豐年多方營辦，防秋之際或乏軍興。

translations.literal: In the third year Henan was quite abundant and the people had stored much grain; Ruli memorialized: "Among state affairs none outweighs food; now garrison troops everywhere increase while building new cities is also costly—if we do not use this abundant year to prepare in many ways, at autumn defense army supplies may fail.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Henan was abundant and the people had stored much grain. Ruli memorialized: "Among state affairs none outweighs food. Garrisons are growing and new cities costly to build. If we do not use this abundant year to prepare, autumn defense may lack supplies.

sentences.zh: 乞于河南州府驗其物價低昂，權宜立式，凡內外四品以下雜正班散官及承廕人，免當暴使監官功酬，或僧道官師德號度牒、寺觀院額等，並聽買之。

translations.literal: I beg that in Henan prefectures prices high and low be verified and an expedient regulation set: all within and outside of fourth rank and below, miscellaneous regular and scattered offices, and yin privilege holders may be exempted from corvée, messenger duty, supervision, official merit rewards, or may purchase Buddhist and Daoist offices, master titles, ordination certificates, temple and monastery plaques, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Henan prefectures verify prices and set an expedient rule: officials of fourth rank and below inside and outside the capital, miscellaneous ranks, and yin privilege holders may buy exemption from corvée and messenger duty or purchase Buddhist and Daoist offices, ordination certificates, temple plaques, and the like.

sentences.zh: 司縣官有能勸誘輸粟至三千石者，將來注授升本榜首，五千石以上遷官一階，萬石以上升職一等，並注見闕。

translations.literal: County officials who can induce grain delivery up to three thousand shi shall at future appointment be ranked first on the promotion list; five thousand shi and above, one rank advancement; ten thousand shi and above, one grade promotion—all registered for current vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: County officials who induce delivery of three thousand shi shall rank first on the next promotion list; five thousand shi, one rank advancement; ten thousand shi, one grade promotion—all registered for current vacancies.

sentences.zh: 庶幾人知勸慕，多所收穫。」

translations.literal: Perhaps people will know encouragement and emulation and much will be collected."
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps people will be encouraged and much grain collected."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 同提舉榷貨司王三錫建議榷油，高琪以用度方急，勸上行之。

translations.literal: Associate Commissioner of the Monopoly Bureau Wang Sanxi proposed monopolizing oil; Gao Qi, because expenditures were urgent, urged the emperor to enact it.
translations.idiomatic: Associate monopoly commissioner Wang Sanxi proposed monopolizing oil; Gao Qi, with expenditures urgent, urged the emperor to enact it.

sentences.zh: 汝礪上言曰：「古無榷法，自漢以來始置鹽鐵酒榷均輸官，以佐經費。

translations.literal: Ruli submitted: "Antiquity had no monopoly law; from Han onward offices for salt, iron, wine monopolies, and equalized transport were established to supplement state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli submitted: "Antiquity had no monopoly law. From Han onward offices for salt, iron, wine monopolies, and equalized transport supplemented state expenses.

sentences.zh: 末流至有算舟車、稅間架，其征利之術固已盡矣，然亦未聞榷油也。

translations.literal: In later ages there came counting boats and carts and taxing building frames—the methods of extracting profit were indeed exhausted, yet never was oil monopolized heard.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages counted boats and carts and taxed building frames—profit-seeking was exhausted—yet never was oil monopolized.

sentences.zh: 蓋油者世所共用，利歸於公則害及於民，故古今皆置不論，亦厭苛細而重煩擾也。

translations.literal: Oil is used by all the world; if profit goes to the state, harm reaches the people—therefore past and present have left it unregulated, also loathing petty severity and heavy harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Oil is used by everyone; if profit goes to the state, harm reaches the people. Past and present have left it alone, loathing petty severity and harassment.

sentences.zh: 國家自軍興，河南一路歲入稅租不啻加倍，又有額征諸錢、橫泛雜役，無非出於民者，而更議榷油，歲收銀數十萬兩。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, Henan Circuit's yearly tax and rent income has been no less than doubled, with fixed levies of various monies and widespread miscellaneous corvée—all from the people—yet now oil monopoly is debated, yearly collecting several hundred thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, Henan tax and rent income has more than doubled, with fixed levies and widespread corvée—all from the people—yet now oil monopoly is debated for several hundred thousand taels yearly.

sentences.zh: 夫國以民為本，當此之際，民可以重困乎！

translations.literal: The state takes the people as foundation—at such a time, can the people be heavily afflicted?
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on the people—at such a time, can they be crushed further?

sentences.zh: 若從三錫議，是以舉世通行之貨為榷貨，私家常用之物為禁物，自古不行之法為良法，切為聖朝不取也。

translations.literal: If Sanxi's proposal is followed, goods circulating throughout the world become monopoly goods, household daily necessities become forbidden goods, and methods never used since antiquity become good law—this is truly not for our sage dynasty to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: If Sanxi's proposal is followed, universal goods become monopoly goods, daily household necessities become forbidden goods, and methods never used since antiquity become good law—our sage dynasty should not adopt this.

sentences.zh: 若果行之，其害有五，臣請言之：河南州縣當立務九百餘所，設官千八百餘員，而胥隸工作之徒不與焉。

translations.literal: If truly enacted, harms are five—I beg to state them: Henan prefectures and counties would establish over nine hundred stations and over eighteen hundred officials, not counting clerks and laborers.
translations.idiomatic: If enacted, there are five harms. Henan would establish over nine hundred stations and over eighteen hundred officials, not counting clerks and laborers.

sentences.zh: 費既不貲，而又創構屋宇，奪買作具，公私俱擾，殆不勝言。

translations.literal: Costs are already unaffordable, yet new buildings would be erected and tools seized or bought—public and private alike disturbed, scarcely to be described.
translations.idiomatic: Costs are already unaffordable, yet new buildings would be erected and tools seized—the public and private sectors alike disturbed beyond description.

sentences.zh: 至於提點官司有升降決罰之法，其課一虧，必生抑配之弊，小民受病，益不能堪，其害一也。

translations.literal: As for supervisory offices with promotion, demotion, and penalty rules—if quotas fall short once, forced allocation abuses surely arise; common people suffer and can less bear it—first harm.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory offices have promotion and penalty rules; if quotas fall short, forced allocation abuses arise and common people suffer unbearably. First harm.

sentences.zh: 夫油之貴賤所在不齊，惟其商旅轉販有無相易，所以其價常平，人易得之。

translations.literal: Oil's price high and low differs by place; only because merchants transport and trade abundance and scarcity do prices stay level and people easily obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Oil prices differ by region; merchants transport and trade to balance supply, so prices stay level and people obtain oil easily.

sentences.zh: 今既設官各有分地，輒相侵犯者有罪，是使貴處常貴而賤處常賤，其害二也。

translations.literal: Now with officials each having allotted territory, crossing boundaries is criminal—expensive places stay expensive and cheap places cheap—second harm.
translations.idiomatic: With officials each allotted territory, crossing boundaries is criminal—expensive regions stay expensive and cheap regions cheap. Second harm.

sentences.zh: 民家日用不能躬自沽之，而轉鬻者增取利息，則價不得不貴，而用不得不難，其害三也。

translations.literal: Households cannot buy daily needs themselves; resellers add interest—prices must rise and use grow hard—third harm.
translations.idiomatic: Households cannot buy for themselves; resellers add markup—prices rise and use grows difficult. Third harm.

sentences.zh: 鹽、鐵、酒、醋，公私所造不同，易於分別，惟油不然，莫可辨記。

translations.literal: Salt, iron, wine, and vinegar differ in public and private manufacture and are easy to distinguish—only oil is not, and cannot be marked and identified.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, iron, wine, and vinegar differ in public and private manufacture and are easy to distinguish—oil cannot be marked and identified.

sentences.zh: 今私造者有刑，捕告者有賞，則無賴輩因之得以誣構良民枉陷於罪，其害四也。

translations.literal: Now private manufacture is punished and informers rewarded—ruffians may thereby frame good people in false crimes—fourth harm.
translations.idiomatic: Private manufacture is punished and informers rewarded—ruffians may frame good people. Fourth harm.

sentences.zh: 油戶所置屋宇、作具，用錢已多，有司按業推定物力，以給差賦。

translations.literal: Oil producers' buildings and tools already cost much; offices assess property by trade to assign corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Oil producers' buildings and tools already cost much; offices assess their property for corvée and levies.

sentences.zh: 今奪其具、廢其業而差賦如前，何以自活，其害五也。

translations.literal: Now seizing their tools and ending their trade while corvée stays as before—how may they live?—fifth harm.
translations.idiomatic: Seize their tools and end their trade while corvée stays the same—how can they live? Fifth harm.

sentences.zh: 惟罷之便。」

translations.literal: Only abolition is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Only abolition is wise."

sentences.zh: 上是之，然重違高琪意，乃詔集百官議於尚書省。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, yet loath to oppose Gao Qi's intent, ordered all officials to deliberate at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed but loath to oppose Gao Qi and ordered all officials to deliberate at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書高夔、工部侍郎粘割荊山、知開封府事溫蒂罕二十等二十六人議同高琪，禮部尚書楊雲翼、翰林侍讀學士趙秉文、南京路轉運使趙瑄、吏部侍郎趙伯成、刑部郎中姬世英、右司諫郭著、提舉倉場使時戩皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Gao Kui, Works Vice Minister Niecai Jingshan, Kaifeng Prefect Wenti Han and twenty others—twenty-six in all—agreed with Gao Qi; Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi, Hanlin Reader Zhao Bingwen, Nanjing Transport Commissioner Zhao Xuan, Personnel Vice Minister Zhao Bocheng, Penal Bureau Director Ji Shiying, Right Bureau Remonstrator Guo Zhuo, and Granary Commissioner Shi Ji all deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Gao Kui, Works vice minister Niecai Jingshan, Kaifeng prefect Wenti Han, and twenty-three others—twenty-six in all—agreed with Gao Qi. Minister of Rites Yang Yunyi, Hanlin reader Zhao Bingwen, Nanjing transport commissioner Zhao Xuan, personnel vice minister Zhao Bocheng, penal bureau director Ji Shiying, right bureau remonstrator Guo Zhuo, and granary commissioner Shi Ji all opposed it.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「古所不行者而今行之，是又生一事也，其罷之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What antiquity did not do we now do—this creates yet another affair; abolish it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What antiquity never did we would now do—that creates yet another burden. Abolish it."

sentences.zh: 十月，賜金鼎一，重幣三。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was granted one golden tripod and three sets of heavy silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was granted one golden tripod and three sets of heavy silks.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，拜平章政事，俄而進拜尚書右丞相，監修國史，封壽國公。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor; soon after advanced to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, supervising compilation of the national history, enfeoffed as Duke of Shou State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year (1216) he was appointed grand councilor; soon after he became right chancellor of the Secretariat, supervised compilation of the national history, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shou.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，上表乞致政，不許。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he submitted a memorial begging to retire from government; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year (1217) he asked to retire from government; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 九月，上諭汝礪曰：「昨日視朝，至午方罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor instructed Ruli: "Yesterday at court audience we did not dismiss until noon.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor told Ruli: "Yesterday's court audience did not end until noon.

sentences.zh: 卿老矣，不任久立，奏事畢，用寶之際，可先退坐，恐以勞致疾，反妨議政也。」

translations.literal: You are old and cannot bear long standing; when business is finished, at the moment of applying the seal you may first withdraw and sit, lest labor bring illness and actually hinder deliberation of government."
translations.idiomatic: You are old and cannot stand long. When business is finished, at the moment of applying the seal you may withdraw and sit, lest strain bring illness and hinder government."

sentences.zh: 是月，複乞致仕，上諭之曰：「丞相之禮盡矣，然今廷臣誰如丞相者，而必欲求去乎，姑留輔朕可也。」

translations.literal: That month he again begged to retire; the emperor instructed him: "The chancellor's rites have been fully performed, yet among court ministers today who is like the chancellor that you must seek to leave? For now remain and assist me."
translations.idiomatic: That month he again asked to retire. The emperor told him: "You have received every honor due a chancellor. Among court ministers today, who equals you, that you must leave? Stay and assist me for now."

sentences.zh: 十月，躐遷榮祿大夫，仍諭曰：「丞相數求去，朕以社稷事重，故堅留之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted by leap to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing; the emperor again instructed: "The chancellor has repeatedly sought to leave; I, because state affairs are weighty, have firmly kept him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted by leap to grand master of glorious blessing. The emperor again said: "The chancellor has repeatedly sought to leave; because state affairs are weighty, I have kept him firmly.

sentences.zh: 丞相老矣，而官猶未至二品，故特升兩階。」

translations.literal: The chancellor is old yet his rank had not reached second grade; therefore I specially raised him two steps."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor is old yet his rank had not reached second grade; therefore I raised him two steps."

sentences.zh: 十二月，上複諭曰：「向朕以卿年老，視朝之日侍立為勞，令用寶時退坐廊下，而卿違之，複侍立終朝，豈有司不為設榻耶？

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor again instructed: "Previously I, because you are old, found standing attendance at court laborious and ordered you to withdraw and sit in the corridor when the seal was used—yet you disobeyed and again stood attendance the whole session. Did the offices not provide a couch?
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor again said: "Earlier, because you are old, I found standing at court laborious and ordered you to sit in the corridor when the seal was used—but you disobeyed and stood the whole session. Did the offices not provide a couch?

sentences.zh: 卿其勉從朕意。」

translations.literal: You should strive to follow my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Please do your best to follow my wishes."

sentences.zh: 元光元年四月，汝礪跪奏事，上命起曰：「卿大臣也，所言皆社稷計。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanguang, Ruli knelt to report business; the emperor ordered him to rise, saying: "You are a great minister; what you say is all for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanguang (1222), Ruli knelt to report business. The emperor told him to rise: "You are a great minister; everything you say concerns the state.

sentences.zh: 朕之責卿，惟在盡誠，何事小謹，自今勿複爾也。」

translations.literal: What I require of you is only full sincerity—why petty caution? From now on do not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: All I require of you is full sincerity. Why such petty caution? Do not do so again."

sentences.zh: 七月，上謂宰臣曰：「昔有言世宗太儉者，或曰不爾則安得廣畜積。
