translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor told the chief ministers: "Formerly some said Shizong was too frugal; others said without that how could there be broad accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor told the chief ministers: "Some once said Shizong was too frugal; others said without that how could there be broad reserves.

sentences.zh: 章宗時用度甚多，而得不闕乏者，蓋先朝有以遺之也。」

translations.literal: In Zhangzong's time expenditures were very great yet nothing was lacking—this was because the former court had bequeathed it."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangzong's time expenditures were great yet nothing ran short—because the former court had left reserves."

sentences.zh: 汝礪因進言曰：「儉乃帝王大德，陛下言及此，天下福也。」

translations.literal: Ruli then advanced: "Frugality is a great virtue of emperors; that Your Majesty speaks of this is fortune for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Ruli added: "Frugality is a great virtue of emperors. That Your Majesty speaks of this is fortune for the realm."

sentences.zh: 九月，上又謂宰臣曰：「有功者雖有微過亦當貸之，無功者豈可貸耶？

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor again told the chief ministers: "Those with merit, though they have minor faults, should be pardoned—can those without merit be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor again told the chief ministers: "Those with merit should be pardoned for minor faults—can those without merit be pardoned?

sentences.zh: 然有功者人喜謗議。

translations.literal: Yet those with merit are what people love to slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yet people love to slander those with merit.

sentences.zh: 凡有以功過言於朕者，朕必深求其實，雖近侍為言不敢輕信，亦未嘗徇一己之愛憎也。」

translations.literal: Whenever anyone speaks to me of merit or fault, I must deeply seek the facts; even when close attendants speak I dare not lightly believe, nor have I ever followed private love or hate."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone speaks to me of merit or fault, I seek the facts deeply. Even close attendants I do not lightly believe, nor do I follow private likes or dislikes."

sentences.zh: 汝礪因對曰：「公生明，偏生暗。

translations.literal: Ruli replied: "Impartiality breeds clarity; partiality breeds darkness.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli replied: "Impartiality breeds clarity; partiality breeds darkness.

sentences.zh: 凡人多徇愛憎，不合公議。

translations.literal: Most people follow private love and hate, not public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Most people follow private likes and dislikes, not public opinion.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖明，故能如是耳。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage—therefore you can be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage—that is why you can act thus."

sentences.zh: 二年正月，複乞致政，上面諭曰：「今若從卿，始終之道俱盡，于卿甚安，在朕亦為美事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year he again begged to retire from government; the emperor instructed him face to face: "If I now follow you, the way from start to finish is complete—for you it is very peaceful, for me also a fine matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he again asked to retire. The emperor told him: "If I grant this now, your path from start to finish is complete—for you it is peaceful, for me also a fine thing.

sentences.zh: 但時方多故，而朕複不德，正賴舊人輔佐，故未能遂卿高志耳。」

translations.literal: But troubles are many and I am again without virtue; I rely on old men to assist, and therefore cannot fulfill your lofty wish."
translations.idiomatic: But troubles are many and I lack virtue; I rely on old servants to assist and cannot fulfill your wish."

sentences.zh: 汝礪固辭，竟不許，因謂曰：「朕每聞人有所毀譽，必求其實。」

translations.literal: Ruli firmly declined but was not permitted; the emperor then said: "Whenever I hear someone praised or slandered, I must seek the facts."
translations.idiomatic: Ruli firmly declined but was refused. The emperor then said: "Whenever I hear praise or slander, I seek the facts."

sentences.zh: 汝礪對曰：「昔齊威王封即墨大夫，烹阿大夫及左右之嘗毀譽者，由是群臣恐懼，莫敢飾非，齊國大治。

translations.literal: Ruli replied: "Formerly King Wei of Qi enfeoffed the prefect of Jimo and boiled the prefect of A and those around him who had slandered and praised—thereafter the ministers feared and none dared conceal wrong; Qi was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli replied: "King Wei of Qi enfeoffed the prefect of Jimo and executed the prefect of A and those who had slandered and praised—thereafter ministers feared to conceal wrong and Qi was well governed.

sentences.zh: 陛下言及此，治安可期也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty speaks of this—order and peace may be expected."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty speaks of this—order and peace may be expected."

sentences.zh: 二月，上以汝礪年高，免朝拜，侍立久則憩于殿下，仍敕有司設榻焉。

translations.literal: In the second month, because Ruli was old, the emperor exempted him from court obeisance; when standing attendance was long he might rest below the hall, and offices were still ordered to provide a couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, because Ruli was old, the emperor exempted him from court obeisance; when attendance was long he might rest below the hall, and offices were ordered to provide a couch.

sentences.zh: 三月，又乞致仕，複優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the third month he again begged to retire; again a gracious edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he again asked to retire; again a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「人有才堪任事，而處心不正者，終不足貴。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the assembled ministers: "A man may have talent fit for office yet if his heart is not upright, in the end he is not to be prized."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers: "A man may have talent for office yet if his heart is not upright, he is not to be prized in the end."

sentences.zh: 汝礪對曰：「其心不正而濟之以才，所謂虎而翼者也，雖古聖人亦未易知。」

translations.literal: Ruli replied: "If the heart is not upright yet aided by talent, this is what is called giving wings to a tiger—even ancient sages were not easy to know."
translations.idiomatic: Ruli replied: "An un upright heart aided by talent is giving wings to a tiger—even ancient sages were hard to read."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed this so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 他日複謂宰臣曰：「凡人處心善良而行事忠實，斯為難得。

translations.literal: Another day he again told the chief ministers: "When a person keeps a kind heart and acts faithfully, this is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he told the chief ministers: "A kind heart and faithful conduct are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 若言巧心偽，亦複何用。

translations.literal: If words are clever and the heart false, what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: Clever words and a false heart are useless.

sentences.zh: 然善良者，人又多目為平常。」

translations.literal: Yet kind people are often seen by others as ordinary."
translations.idiomatic: Yet kind people are often seen as ordinary."

sentences.zh: 汝礪對曰：「人材少全，亦隨其所長取之耳。」

translations.literal: Ruli replied: "Human talent is rarely complete; one takes what each excels in."
translations.idiomatic: Ruli replied: "Talent is rarely complete; take what each excels in."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 五月，上問宰執以修完京城樓櫓事，汝礪奏：「所用皆大木，顧今難得，方令計置。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor asked the chief executives about repairing the capital's towers and ramparts; Ruli memorialized: "What is used is all great timber, but now it is hard to obtain—we are ordering plans."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor asked about repairing the capital's towers and ramparts. Ruli reported: "Great timber is required but hard to obtain—we are arranging supply."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕宮中別殿有可用者即用之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In my palace's separate halls, whatever is usable, use it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Use whatever usable timber is in my palace's separate halls."

sentences.zh: 汝礪對以不宜毀，上曰：「所居之外，毀亦何害，不愈于勞民遠致乎！」

translations.literal: Ruli replied that destruction was inappropriate; the emperor said: "Beyond where I dwell, what harm in destroying? Is it not better than laboring the people to bring it from afar!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruli said destruction was inappropriate. The emperor said: "Beyond where I dwell, what harm? Is that not better than laboring the people to bring timber from afar!"

sentences.zh: 哀宗初即位，諫官言汝礪欺君固位，天下所共嫉，宜黜之以厲百官。

translations.literal: When Aizong first took the throne, remonstrating officials said Ruli deceived the ruler and clung to office, hated by all under heaven, and should be dismissed to warn the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong first took the throne, remonstrators said Ruli deceived the ruler and clung to office, hated throughout the realm, and should be dismissed to warn officials.

sentences.zh: 哀宗曰：「昔惠帝言，我不如高帝，當守先帝法耳。

translations.literal: Aizong said: "Formerly Emperor Hui said, I am not equal to Emperor Gao—I should keep the former emperor's laws.
translations.idiomatic: Aizong said: "Emperor Hui once said he was not equal to Emperor Gao and should keep the former emperor's laws.

sentences.zh: 汝礪乃先帝立以為相者，又可黜歟！」

translations.literal: Ruli was whom the former emperor installed as chancellor—how can he be dismissed!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruli was whom the former emperor installed as chancellor—how can he be dismissed!"

sentences.zh: 又有投匿名書雲：「高某不退當殺之。」

translations.literal: There was also an anonymous letter saying: "If Gao does not retire he should be killed."
translations.idiomatic: An anonymous letter also said: "If Gao does not retire, kill him."

sentences.zh: 汝礪因是告老，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Ruli therefore reported old age; a gracious edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli therefore reported old age; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 正大元年三月，薨，年七十一，配享宣宗廟。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhengda he died, age seventy-one, with temple sacrifice at Xuanzong's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Zhengda (1224) he died at seventy-one and received temple sacrifice at Xuanzong's shrine.

sentences.zh: 為人慎密廉潔，能結人主知，然規守格法，循嘿避事，故為相十餘年未嘗有譴訶。

translations.literal: As a man he was cautious, secretive, incorrupt, and able to win the ruler's trust, yet he observed regulations, kept silent and avoided affairs—therefore as chancellor more than ten years he never received reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious, incorrupt, and won the ruler's trust, yet he observed regulations, kept silent, and avoided controversy—so as chancellor for more than ten years he never received reprimand.

sentences.zh: 貪戀不去，當時士論頗以為譏雲。

translations.literal: Greedy clinging and not leaving—contemporary scholarly opinion rather criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: His greedy clinging to office drew criticism from scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 張行信

translations.literal: Zhang Xingxin
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingxin

sentences.zh: 張行信，字信甫，先名行忠，避莊獻太子諱改焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingxin, style name Xinfu, formerly named Xingzhong, changed to avoid the taboo of Crown Prince Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingxin, whose style name was Xinfu, was formerly named Xingzhong and changed his name to avoid the taboo of Crown Prince Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 行簡弟也。

translations.literal: He was the younger brother of Xingjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was the younger brother of Zhang Xingjian.

sentences.zh: 登大定二十八年進士第，累官銅山令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading and rose through offices to magistrate of Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the twenty-eighth year of Dading (1188) and rose to magistrate of Tongshan.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，以廉擢授監察禦史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang he was promoted for integrity to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang (1190) he was promoted for integrity to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，同知山東西路轉運使，俄簽河東路按察司事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was Vice Transport Commissioner of Shandong West Circuit; soon after he signed affairs of the Hedong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe (1203) he was vice transport commissioner of Shandong West Circuit; soon after he signed affairs on the Hedong surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，召見於泰和殿，行信因言二事，一依舊移轉吏目以除民害，一徐、邳地下宜麥，稅粟許納麥以便民。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year he was summoned to the Taihe Hall; Xingxin then spoke on two matters: first, to transfer clerks according to old practice to remove harm to the people; second, that in Xu and Pi the soil suits wheat and grain tax should permit wheat payment for the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year he was summoned to the Taihe Hall and proposed two reforms: restore the old practice of rotating clerks to curb abuses, and in Xu and Pi allow wheat in place of grain tax because the soil suits wheat.

sentences.zh: 上是其言，令尚書省議行之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and ordered the Secretariat to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the Secretariat to implement both proposals.

sentences.zh: 崇慶二年，為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongqing he became Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongqing (1213) he became left remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 時胡沙虎已除名為民，賂遺權貴，將複進用。

translations.literal: At that time Hu Shahu had been struck from the rolls and made a commoner, bribing powerful nobles and about to be reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu had been struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status; he was bribing powerful nobles and about to be reemployed.

sentences.zh: 舉朝無敢言者，行信乃上章曰：「胡沙虎殘忍凶悖，跋扈強梁，媚結近習，以圖稱譽。

translations.literal: The whole court dared not speak; Xingxin then submitted a memorial: "Hu Shahu is cruel, fierce, and rebellious, overbearing and violent, fawning on those close to the ruler to seek praise.
translations.idiomatic: No one in court dared speak. Xingxin memorialized: "Hu Shahu is cruel, fierce, and rebellious, overbearing and violent, fawning on the ruler's intimates to win praise.

sentences.zh: 自其廢黜，士庶莫不忻悅。

translations.literal: Since his dismissal, officials and commoners have all been glad.
translations.idiomatic: Since his dismissal, officials and commoners alike have rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 今若複用，惟恐為害更甚前日，況利害之機更有大於此者。」

translations.literal: If he is now reemployed, I fear harm will exceed the past; moreover the stakes of gain and loss may be greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: If he is reemployed, harm may exceed the past—and the stakes may be even greater."

sentences.zh: 書再上，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted again; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 及胡沙虎弑逆，人甚危之，行信坦然不顧也。

translations.literal: When Hu Shahu committed regicide many were greatly alarmed for him; Xingxin was calm and unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Shahu committed regicide many feared for Xingxin; he remained calm and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，宣宗即位，改元貞祐。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month Emperor Xuanzong took the throne and changed the era name to Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month Xuanzong took the throne and changed the era name to Zhenyou.

sentences.zh: 行信以皇嗣未立，無以系天下之望，上疏曰：「自古人君即位，必立太子以為儲副，必下詔以告中外。

translations.literal: Xingxin, because the imperial heir had not been established and there was no way to bind the hopes of the empire, submitted a memorial: "From antiquity when rulers succeed to the throne they must establish an heir apparent as reserve successor and must issue edicts to announce it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Because no imperial heir had been named to sustain the people's hopes, Xingxin memorialized: "Since antiquity, when a ruler succeeds to the throne he must establish an heir apparent and issue edicts to announce it at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 竊見皇長子每遇趨朝，用東宮儀衛，及至丹墀，還列諸王班。

translations.literal: I have seen the eldest imperial son whenever he attends court use Eastern Palace guards and regalia, yet upon reaching the red steps he still ranks among the princes' formation.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the eldest imperial son attend court with Eastern Palace guards and regalia, yet upon reaching the red steps he still ranks with the other princes.

sentences.zh: 況已除侍臣，而今未定其禮，可謂名不正言不順矣。

translations.literal: Moreover he has already been appointed attendant minister, yet his rites are still unsettled—this may be called improper naming and unsound speech.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he has already been appointed an attendant minister, yet his ceremonial status remains unsettled—truly, the name is not correct and the words do not accord.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝元年，首立子啟為太子者，所以尊祖廟、重社稷也。

translations.literal: Formerly in the first year of Han Emperor Wen, when he first established his son Qi as heir apparent, it was to honor the ancestral temples and esteem the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Emperor Wen first established his son Qi as heir apparent in his first year, it was to honor the ancestral temples and uphold the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 願與大臣詳議，酌前代故事，早下明詔，以定其位，慎選宮僚，輔成德器，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I wish to deliberate in detail with great ministers, consider precedents of former ages, and early issue a clear edict to fix his position, carefully select palace staff to nurture his virtue and capacity—then the empire would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty deliberate with the great ministers, consult precedents from former ages, and issue a clear edict soon to fix his position, carefully select palace staff to nurture his virtue and capacity—the empire would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎誅，上封事言正刑賞，辭載《胡沙虎傳》。

translations.literal: After Hu Shahu was executed, he submitted a sealed memorial on correcting punishments and rewards—the text is in the biography of Hu Shahu.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Shahu was executed, he submitted a sealed memorial on correcting punishments and rewards—the text appears in the biography of Hu Shahu.

sentences.zh: 又言：「自兵興以來，將帥甚難其人，願陛下令重臣各舉所知，才果可用，即賜召見，褒顯獎諭，令其自效，必有奮命報國者。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since war arose, finding commanders has been very difficult; I beg Your Majesty to order great ministers each to recommend those they know—if talent is truly usable, summon and praise them, let them prove themselves, and there will surely be those who strive with their lives for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Since the wars began, good commanders have been hard to find. I beg Your Majesty to have great ministers each recommend men they know. If talent proves usable, summon them, praise them, and let them prove themselves—some will surely give their lives for the state.

sentences.zh: 昔李牧為趙將，軍功爵賞皆得自專，出攻入守不從中覆，遂能北破大敵，西抑強秦。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Mu as Zhao's general controlled military merit and rewards himself; going out to attack and in to defend without central reversal—thus he could north defeat a great enemy and west restrain powerful Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu as Zhao's general controlled rewards himself and attacked and defended without interference from the center—thus he defeated great enemies in the north and checked powerful Qin in the west.

sentences.zh: 今命將若不以文法拘繩、中旨牽制，委任責成，使得盡其智能，則克復之功可望矣。」

translations.literal: Now if commanders are not bound by documents and law nor pulled by central edicts, but entrusted with responsibility so they may fully use their intelligence, then recovery may be hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: If commanders are not bound by paperwork and central edicts but entrusted with full responsibility to use their abilities, recovery may be hoped for."

sentences.zh: 上善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 時方擢任王守信、賈耐兒者為將，皆鄙俗不材、不曉兵律。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shouxin, Jia Naier, and others were being promoted as generals—all vulgar, untalented, ignorant of military law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouxin, Jia Naier, and others were being promoted as generals—all vulgar, untalented men ignorant of military law.

sentences.zh: 行信懼其誤國，上疏曰：「《易》稱'開國承家，小人勿用'。

translations.literal: Xingxin feared they would harm the state and memorialized: "The Changes says 'In founding a state and sustaining a house, do not employ petty men.'
translations.idiomatic: Xingxin feared they would harm the state and memorialized: "The Book of Changes says, 'In founding a state and sustaining a house, do not employ petty men.'

sentences.zh: 聖人所以垂戒後世者，其嚴如此。

translations.literal: The severity with which the sage warned posterity is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's warning to posterity was that strict.

sentences.zh: 今大兵縱橫，人情洶懼，應敵興理，非賢智莫能。

translations.literal: Now great armies roam and popular feeling is alarmed; meeting the enemy and restoring order—none but the worthy and wise can do it.
translations.idiomatic: Great armies roam and the people are alarmed; meeting the enemy and restoring order requires wisdom.

sentences.zh: 狂子庸流，猥蒙拔擢，參預機務，甚無謂也。」

translations.literal: Mad fools and vulgar fellows basely receiving promotion and participating in state affairs—this is very pointless."
translations.idiomatic: Mad fools and vulgar men have been promoted to state affairs—this is absurd."

sentences.zh: 於是上皆罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor dismissed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed them all.

sentences.zh: 權元帥右都監內族訛可率兵五千護糧通州，遇兵輒潰，行信上章曰：「禦兵之道，無過賞罰，使其臨敵有所慕而樂於進，有所畏而不敢退，然後將士用命而功可成。

translations.literal: Acting Marshal Right Director of the Inner Tribe Eke led five thousand men to escort grain to Tongzhou; encountering enemy troops he fled at once. Xingxin memorialized: "The way to control troops is nothing beyond reward and punishment, making them before the enemy have something to admire and advance gladly, something to fear and not dare retreat—then officers and soldiers obey and achievement is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Acting marshal right director Eke of the inner tribe led five thousand men to escort grain to Tongzhou and fled at the first contact. Xingxin memorialized: "Controlling troops is nothing but reward and punishment—give them reason to advance gladly and fear to retreat—then they will obey and success is possible.

sentences.zh: 若訛可敗衄，宜明正其罪，朝廷寬容，一切不問，臣恐禦兵之道未盡也。」

translations.literal: If Eke was defeated, his crime should be clearly fixed; the court has been lenient and asked nothing—I fear the way of controlling troops is not complete."
translations.idiomatic: Eke was defeated and his crime should be clearly punished. The court has been lenient and asked nothing—I fear military discipline is incomplete."

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「卿意具悉，訛可等已下獄矣。」

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Your intent is fully understood; Eke and others are already imprisoned."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Your intent is understood; Eke and others are already imprisoned."

sentences.zh: 時中都受兵，方遣使請和，握兵者畏縮不敢戰，曰：「恐壞和事。」

translations.literal: At that time the central capital was under attack; envoys were being sent to sue for peace; those holding troops shrank back and dared not fight, saying: "We fear harming the peace talks."
translations.idiomatic: The central capital was under attack while envoys sued for peace. Commanders shrank from fighting, saying, "We fear harming peace talks."

sentences.zh: 行信上言：「和與戰二事本不相干，奉使者自專議和，將兵者惟當主戰，豈得以和事為辭。

translations.literal: Xingxin submitted: "Peace and war are originally unrelated; envoys handle peace on their own, commanders should only master war—how can peace be an excuse?
translations.idiomatic: Xingxin submitted: "Peace and war are separate matters. Envoys handle peace; commanders should fight. Peace is no excuse for inaction.

sentences.zh: 自崇慶來，皆以和誤，若我軍時肯進戰，稍挫其鋒，則和事成也久矣。

translations.literal: Since Chongqing all have been misled by peace; if our army had been willing to advance and slightly blunt their edge, peace would have been achieved long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chongqing we have been misled by peace. If our army had fought and blunted the enemy, peace would have been achieved long ago.

sentences.zh: 頃北使既來，然猶破東京，略河東。

translations.literal: Recently northern envoys came, yet they still captured Dongjing and raided Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Northern envoys came, yet the enemy still captured Dongjing and raided Hedong.

sentences.zh: 今我使方行，將帥輒按兵不動，於和議卒無益也。

translations.literal: Now our envoys are just departing yet commanders hold troops motionless—this ultimately does not help peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: Our envoys are just departing while commanders hold their troops still—this does not help peace at all.

sentences.zh: 事勢益急，芻糧益艱，和之成否蓋未可知，豈當閉門坐守以待弊哉。

translations.literal: The situation grows more urgent, fodder and grain more scarce—whether peace succeeds is unknown; how can we shut the gates and sit in defense awaiting exhaustion?
translations.idiomatic: The situation grows urgent and supplies scarcer—whether peace succeeds is unknown. How can we shut the gates and wait to be exhausted?

sentences.zh: 宜及士馬尚壯，擇猛將銳兵，防衛轉輸，往來拒戰，使之少沮，則附近蓄積皆可入京師，和議亦不日可成矣。」

translations.literal: We should while horses and men are still strong choose fierce generals and sharp troops to guard transport, meet the enemy in coming and going battle and somewhat discourage them—then nearby stores can all enter the capital and peace may be achieved within days."
translations.idiomatic: While troops are still strong, choose fierce generals to guard supply lines and fight skirmishes that discourage the enemy—then nearby stores can reach the capital and peace may soon follow."

sentences.zh: 上心知其善而不能行。

translations.literal: The emperor inwardly knew this was good yet could not enact it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew this was sound but could not enact it.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，以朝廷括糧恐失民心，上書言：「近日朝廷令知大興府胥鼎便宜計畫軍食，鼎因奏許人納粟買官。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, fearing that state grain requisition would lose popular hearts, he submitted: "Recently the court ordered Daxing Prefect Xu Ding to plan army food expediently; Ding memorialized permitting people to pay grain to buy office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year (1215), fearing grain requisition would lose popular support, he wrote: "The court ordered Daxing prefect Xu Ding to plan army supplies. Ding allowed people to pay grain for offices.

sentences.zh: 既又遣參知政事奧屯忠孝括官民糧，戶存兩月，餘悉令輸官，酬以爵級銀鈔。

translations.literal: Then Participant in Government Affairs Aotun Zhongxiao was sent to requisition official and private grain—each household kept two months, the rest all delivered to the state, compensated with rank, silver, and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Then participant in government affairs Aotun Zhongxiao was sent to requisition grain—each household kept two months' supply, the rest to the state, paid in rank, silver, and notes.

sentences.zh: 時有粟者或先具數於鼎，未及入官。

translations.literal: Those with grain had sometimes first registered amounts with Ding and not yet delivered to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Some who had grain had already registered amounts with Ding but not yet delivered to the state.

sentences.zh: 忠孝複欲多得以明己功，凡鼎所籍者不除其數，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao again wished to take more to show his merit; all Ding had registered was not deducted from their quota—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiao wanted more to show his merit and did not deduct what Ding had registered—the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 今米價踴貴，無所從糴，民糧止兩月又奪之，將不獨歸咎有司，亦怨朝廷不察也。

translations.literal: Now rice prices soar and there is nowhere to buy; the people's two months' grain is again seized—they will blame not only offices but also resent the court's lack of insight.
translations.idiomatic: Rice prices soar and there is nowhere to buy. Seizing the people's two-month reserve will make them blame officials and resent the court's blindness.

sentences.zh: 大兵在邇，人方危懼，若複無聊，或生他變，則所得不償所損矣。」

translations.literal: Great armies are near and people are alarmed; if further driven to despair, other troubles may arise—the gain will not repay the loss."
translations.idiomatic: Great armies are near and people are alarmed. If driven further to despair, other troubles may arise—the gain will not repay the loss."

sentences.zh: 上深善其言，即命與近臣往審處焉。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved and at once ordered him with close ministers to go investigate and settle it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly approved and ordered him with close ministers to investigate and settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 仍諭忠孝曰：「極知卿盡心於公，然國家本欲得糧，今既得矣，姑從人便可也。」

translations.literal: He also instructed Zhongxiao: "I fully know you devote your heart to the public, yet the state originally wanted grain—now it is obtained; for now follow what is convenient for the people."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Zhongxiao: "I know you serve the public zealously. The state wanted grain and has it. For now, ease the burden on the people."

sentences.zh: 四月，遷山東東路按察使，兼轉運使，仍權本路宣撫副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong East Circuit, also Transport Commissioner, and still acting Pacification Vice Commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he became surveillance commissioner of Shandong East Circuit, also transport commissioner, and acting pacification vice commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 將行，求入見，上禦便殿見之。

translations.literal: Before departing he sought an audience; the emperor received him in the privy hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he sought an audience; the emperor received him in the privy hall.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「臣伏見奧屯忠孝飾詐不忠，臨事慘刻，與胡沙虎為黨。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your servant humbly observes Aotun Zhongxiao displays deceit and disloyalty, is harsh in affairs, and was Hu Shahu's partisan."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "I observe that Aotun Zhongxiao is deceitful and disloyal, harsh in affairs, and was Hu Shahu's partisan."

sentences.zh: 歷數其罪，且曰：「無事時猶不容一相非才，況今多故，可使斯人與政乎？

translations.literal: He listed his crimes and said: "In peaceful times one unfit chancellor was not tolerated—how in today's many troubles can such a man participate in government?
translations.idiomatic: He listed Zhongxiao's crimes and said: "In peaceful times an unfit chancellor was not tolerated—how in today's troubles can such a man govern?

sentences.zh: 願即罷之。」

translations.literal: I beg he be dismissed at once."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be dismissed at once."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕始即位，進退大臣自當以禮，卿語其親知，諷令求去可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have just taken the throne; advancing and retiring great ministers should follow ritual. Tell his close friends to hint that he should request to leave."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have just taken the throne; dismissing great ministers must follow ritual. Tell his friends to hint that he should resign."

sentences.zh: 行信以告右司郎中把胡魯白忠孝，忠孝不恤也。

translations.literal: Xingxin told Right Bureau Director Bahulu to inform Zhongxiao; Zhongxiao paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxin told right bureau director Bahulu to inform Zhongxiao; Zhongxiao paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，改安武軍節度使，兼冀州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he was changed to Military Commissioner of Anwu Army, also Observation Commissioner within Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year (1216) he became military commissioner of Anwu Army and observation commissioner within Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 始至，即上書言四事，其一曰：「楊安兒賊党旦暮成擒，蓋不足慮。

translations.literal: On first arrival he submitted on four matters; the first said: "Yang An'er's band will be captured morning or evening—hardly worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he submitted four proposals. The first: "Yang An'er's band will soon be captured—hardly worth worry.

sentences.zh: 今日之急，惟在收人心而已。

translations.literal: Today's urgency is only winning people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Today's urgency is only winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 向者官軍討賦，不分善惡，一概誅夷，劫其資產，掠其婦女，重使居民疑畏，逃聚山林。

translations.literal: Formerly government troops collecting levies made no distinction of good and evil, killing all alike, seizing assets and carrying off women—greatly making residents suspicious and afraid, fleeing to gather in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops collecting levies made no distinction between good and evil, killed indiscriminately, seized property, and abducted women—driving residents to flee into the hills.

sentences.zh: 今宜明敕有司，嚴為約束，毋令劫掠平民。

translations.literal: Now offices should be clearly ordered to strictly restrain troops and forbid plundering civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Offices should be clearly ordered to forbid troops from plundering civilians.

sentences.zh: 如此則百姓無不安之心，奸人誑脅之計不行，其勢漸消矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the people will have no unsettled hearts, schemers' plans to deceive and coerce will fail, and their power will gradually fade."
translations.idiomatic: Then the people will be reassured, schemes to deceive and coerce will fail, and the rebels' power will fade."

sentences.zh: 其二曰：「自兵亂之後，郡縣官豪，多能糾集義徒，摧擊土寇，朝廷雖授以本處職任，未幾遣人代之。

translations.literal: The second said: "Since military disorder, county and prefectural magnates have often gathered righteous followers to crush local bandits; though the court grants them local posts, before long others are sent to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: The second: "Since the wars, local magnates have often rallied militias to crush bandits. Though the court grants them local posts, they are soon replaced.

sentences.zh: 夫舊者人所素服，新者未必皆才，緩急之間，啟釁敗事。

translations.literal: The old are what people long obeyed; the new are not necessarily all talented—in urgent moments this breeds trouble and defeats affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The old officials are what people trust; replacements are not necessarily capable—in a crisis this breeds trouble.

sentences.zh: 自今郡縣闕員，乞令尚書省選人擬注。

translations.literal: From now on when prefectures and counties have vacancies, I beg the Secretariat choose men for nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth when prefectures and counties have vacancies, let the Secretariat nominate candidates.

sentences.zh: 其舊官，民便安者宜就加任使，如資級未及，令攝其職，待有功則正授。

translations.literal: For old officials whom the people find comfortable, they should be promoted in place; if rank is not yet sufficient, let them act in the post and upon merit grant regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Old officials whom the people trust should be kept or promoted; if rank is insufficient, let them act in the post and grant regular appointment after merit.

sentences.zh: 庶幾人盡其才，事易以立。」

translations.literal: Perhaps all may fully use their talents and affairs be easy to establish."
translations.idiomatic: Then all may use their talents and affairs will be easier to accomplish."

sentences.zh: 其三曰：「掌軍官敢進戰者十無一二，其或有之，即當責以立功，不宜更授他職。」

translations.literal: The third said: "Officers in command who dare advance to battle are not one or two in ten; if any exist, they should be charged to achieve merit and not be given other posts."
translations.idiomatic: The third: "Few commanders dare fight. Those who do should be pressed for merit, not given other posts."

sentences.zh: 其四曰：「山東軍儲皆鬻爵所獲，及或持敕牒求仕，選曹以等級有不當鬻者往往駁退。

translations.literal: The fourth said: "Shandong army stores all come from selling offices; some hold edicts seeking appointment, and the selection office often rejects those whose rank should not have been sold.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth: "Shandong army stores come from selling offices. Some hold edicts for appointment; the selection office often rejects ranks that should not have been sold.

sentences.zh: 夫鬻所不當，有司罪也，彼何責焉。

translations.literal: Selling what should not be sold is the offices' crime—how blame them?
translations.idiomatic: Selling improper ranks is the offices' fault—why blame the buyers?

sentences.zh: 況海岱重地，群寇未平，田野無所收，倉廩無所積，一旦軍餉不給，複欲鬻爵，其誰信之？」

translations.literal: Moreover the sea and Mount Tai region is weighty ground, bandits not yet pacified, fields yield nothing, granaries store nothing—if army pay fails once and offices are sold again, who will believe it?"
translations.idiomatic: The sea-Tai region is vital; bandits are not pacified; fields and granaries are empty. If pay fails and you sell offices again, who will believe it?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷多用其議。

translations.literal: The court largely adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 八月，召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was summoned as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was summoned as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 九月，改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十二月，轉禮部尚書，兼同修國史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to Minister of Rites, also co-compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he became minister of rites and co-compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，為太子少保，兼前職。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, retaining his previous posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year he became junior guardian of the heir apparent, keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 時尚書省奏：「遼東宣撫副使完顏海奴言，參議官王澮嘗言，本朝紹高辛，黃帝之後也。

translations.literal: Then the Ministry of State submitted: "The Liaodong Pacification vice-commissioner Wanyan Hainu said that the deliberation officer Wang Huan once stated that our dynasty succeeds Gaoxin and is descended from the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry reported: "Liaodong vice-commissioner Wanyan Hainu said deliberation officer Wang Huan had claimed the dynasty succeeds Gaoxin and descends from the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖陶唐，唐祖老子，皆為立廟。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's ancestor was Yao of Tang and Tang's ancestor was Laozi—temples were erected for both.
translations.idiomatic: Han claimed Yao of Tang; Tang claimed Laozi—both had temples built.

sentences.zh: 我朝迄今百年，不為黃帝立廟，無乃愧于漢、唐乎！」

translations.literal: Our dynasty until now a century, no temple erected for the Yellow Emperor—are we not shamed before Han and Tang!"
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty is a century old and has no temple to the Yellow Emperor—is this not a shame beside Han and Tang!"

sentences.zh: 又雲：「本朝初興，旗幟尚赤，其為火德明矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "When our dynasty first rose, banners favored red—its being the virtue of Fire is clear.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "At the dynasty's founding, red banners were favored—the Fire virtue is obvious.

sentences.zh: 主德之祀，闕而不講，亦非禮經重祭祀之意。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to the dynastic virtue is omitted and not discussed—this too is not the meaning of the classics' emphasis on sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Omitting sacrifice to the dynastic virtue ignores what the ritual classics stress about worship.

sentences.zh: 臣聞於澮者如此，乞朝廷議其事。」

translations.literal: What Your servant heard from Huan is thus; I beg the court to deliberate the matter."
translations.idiomatic: This is what I heard from Huan; I ask the court to consider it."

sentences.zh: 詔問有司，行信奏曰：「按《始祖實錄》止稱自高麗而來，未聞出於高辛。

translations.literal: An edict questioned the offices; Xingxin memorialized: "According to the Veritable Records of the Founding Ancestor, it only states coming from Goryeo—nothing is heard of descending from Gaoxin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the ministries; Xingxin replied: "The Founding Ancestor's Veritable Records say only that he came from Goryeo—nowhere that he descended from Gaoxin.

sentences.zh: 今所據欲立黃帝廟，黃帝高辛之祖，借曰紹之，當為木德，今乃言火德，亦何謂也？

translations.literal: Now the grounds cited for wishing to erect a Yellow Emperor temple—the Yellow Emperor is Gaoxin's ancestor; even if we say we succeed him, it should be the virtue of Wood; yet now Fire virtue is spoken—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: The proposal rests on building a Yellow Emperor temple; the Yellow Emperor was Gaoxin's forebear—if we claim that succession, the virtue should be Wood, not Fire. What sense does that make?

sentences.zh: 況國初太祖有訓，因完顏部多尚白，又取金之不變，乃以大金為國號，未嘗議及德運。

translations.literal: Moreover at the founding the Grand Ancestor had instruction: because the Wanyan clan mostly favored white, and taking gold's imperishability, he took Great Jin as the dynastic name—virtue and fate were never discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the founding Grand Ancestor taught: the Wanyan favored white; gold does not tarnish—hence Great Jin as the name. Dynastic virtue was never debated.

sentences.zh: 近章宗朝始集百僚議之，而以繼亡宋火行之絕，定為土德，以告宗廟而詔天下焉。

translations.literal: Recently in Emperor Zhangzong's reign the hundred officials were first assembled to debate it, and by succeeding the extinguished Song's broken Fire line, Earth virtue was fixed, announced to the ancestral temple, and proclaimed to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Zhangzong did officials finally debate it and fix Earth virtue—succeeding the extinguished Song's Fire line—announcing it at the ancestral temple and proclaiming it to the realm.

sentences.zh: 顧澮所言特狂妄者耳。」

translations.literal: As for what Huan said—it is merely reckless talk."
translations.idiomatic: Huan's words are simply reckless."

sentences.zh: 上是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，上將祔享太廟，詔依世宗十六拜之禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, as the emperor was to enshrine and offer at the Grand Ancestral Temple, an edict ordered following Emperor Shizong's sixteen-bows ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, before enshrining tablets in the grand ancestral temple, the emperor ordered Shizong's sixteen-bow rite followed.

sentences.zh: 行信與禮官參定儀注，上言宜從四十四拜之禮，上嘉納焉，語在《禮志》。

translations.literal: Xingxin with the ritual officers jointly fixed the ceremony; he submitted that the forty-four-bows ritual should be followed; the emperor commendably accepted—the account is in the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxin and the ritual officers drafted the rites and urged the forty-four-bow ceremony; the emperor accepted with praise—details are in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，賜行信寶券二萬貫、重幣下端，諭之曰：「太廟拜禮，朕初欲依世宗所行，卿進奏章，備述隨室讀祝，殊為中理。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was complete, Xingxin was granted twenty thousand strings of treasure notes and heavy silks of lower grade; he was instructed: "The ancestral temple bowing ritual—I at first wished to follow what Shizong practiced; you submitted a memorial fully describing reading the prayer at each chamber—it is quite reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: After the rite, he received twenty thousand strings in treasure notes and fine silks. The emperor said: "For the temple bows I first meant to follow Shizong, but your memorial on reading prayers at each chamber was entirely sound.

sentences.zh: 向非卿言，朕幾失之，故特以是旌賞，自今每事更宜盡心。」

translations.literal: But for your words, I would nearly have missed it; therefore I specially reward you thus—from now on in every matter you should even more fully apply your heart."
translations.idiomatic: Without you I would have erred; this reward is in recognition. Henceforth give your utmost in every affair."

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，行信以父暐卒，去官。

translations.literal: That year's twelfth month, Xingxin because his father Wei died left office.
translations.idiomatic: That December Xingxin left office upon his father Wei's death.

sentences.zh: 興定元年三月，起復舊職，權參知政事。

translations.literal: Xingding year 1, third month, he was recalled to his former post, acting as participation grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xingding 1 he was recalled to his old post as acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 六月，真拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Sixth month, formally appointed participation grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was formally appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 時高琪為相，專權用事，惡不附己者，衣冠之士，動遭窘辱，惟行信屢引舊制力抵其非。

translations.literal: Then Gao Qi was chief minister, monopolizing power—he hated those not aligned with him; men of the cap and gown constantly met disgrace; only Xingxin repeatedly citing old regulations strenuously resisted his wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi was chief minister and monopolized power, punishing dissent. Scholar-officials were humiliated at every turn; only Xingxin repeatedly invoked precedent to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 會宋兵侵境，朝廷議遣使詳問，高琪等以為失體，行信獨上疏曰：「今以遣使為不當，臣切惑之。

translations.literal: When Song troops invaded the border, the court debated sending envoys to inquire in detail; Gao Qi and others thought it loss of dignity; Xingxin alone submitted: "Now to deem sending envoys improper—your servant is deeply puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces raided the border, the court debated dispatching envoys; Gao Qi called it demeaning. Xingxin alone memorialized: "I am baffled that sending envoys should be deemed improper.

sentences.zh: 議者不過曰：'遣使則為先示弱，其或不報，報而不遜，則愈失國體。

translations.literal: Those debating say nothing beyond: 'Sending envoys means showing weakness first; if they do not reply, or reply without deference, national dignity is lost the more.'
translations.idiomatic: Critics say only: 'Envoys show weakness first; no reply, or an impertinent one, shames us further.'

sentences.zh: '臣獨以為不然。

translations.literal: Your servant alone thinks not so.
translations.idiomatic: I disagree.

sentences.zh: 彼幸吾釁隙，數肆侵掠，邊臣以兵卻之複來，我大國不責以辭而敵以兵，茲非示弱乎。

translations.literal: They exploit our gaps and repeatedly raid; border officers beat them back yet they come again—we a great state do not hold them to account with words but meet the enemy with troops—is this not showing weakness?
translations.idiomatic: They exploit our divisions and raid repeatedly; our borders repel them only to see them return—we rebuke with arms, not words. Is that not weakness?

sentences.zh: 至於問而不報，報而不遜，曲自在彼，何損於我。

translations.literal: As for inquiry without reply, or reply without deference—the fault lies with them; what harm to us?
translations.idiomatic: If they ignore inquiry or answer rudely, the fault is theirs—not ours.

sentences.zh: 昔大定之初，彼嘗犯順，世宗雖遣丞相烏者行省於汴，實令元帥撒合輦先為辭詰之，彼遂伏罪。

translations.literal: Formerly at the start of Dading they once violated order; Shizong though dispatching the chief minister Wuzhe as provincial commissioner to Bian, actually had the marshal Sahelian first lodge verbal challenge—they then submitted to guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading they violated the peace. Shizong sent chief minister Wuzhe to Bian as commissioner but had Marshal Sahelian challenge them first—and they confessed their fault.

sentences.zh: 其後宋主奪取國書，朝廷複欲加兵，丞相婁室獨以為不可，及刑部尚書梁肅銜命以往，尋亦屈焉。

translations.literal: Afterward the Song ruler seized the state letter; the court again wished to add troops; chief minister Lou Shi alone thought it impossible; when Minister of Justice Liang Su went bearing orders, soon they also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Song emperor seized our state letter; the court again wanted force. Only chief minister Lou Shi objected; Minister of Justice Liang Su went with orders—and Song yielded.

sentences.zh: 在章宗時，倡狂最甚，猶先理問而後用兵。

translations.literal: In Zhangzong's time, when insolence was greatest, still inquiry came first and troops after.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Zhangzong, at their most arrogant, inquiry preceded arms.

sentences.zh: 然則遣使詳問正國家故事，何失體之有。

translations.literal: Then sending envoys to inquire in detail is precisely the state's established practice—where is loss of dignity?
translations.idiomatic: Detailed inquiry by envoy is established practice—how is that a loss of dignity?

sentences.zh: 且國步多艱，戍兵滋久，不思所以休息之，如民力何。

translations.literal: Moreover the state's course is full of hardship, garrison troops prolonged—if we do not consider how to give rest, what of the people's strength?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is hard-pressed and garrisons long deployed—we must find relief for the people.

sentences.zh: 臣書生無甚高論，然事當機會，不敢不罄其愚，惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Your servant a bookish man without lofty discourse, yet the matter meets its moment—I dare not withhold my folly; may Your Majesty examine it."
translations.idiomatic: I am only a scholar without grand theories, but the moment demands speech—I offer my humble view for Your Majesty's consideration."

sentences.zh: 上複令尚書省議，高琪等奏：「行信所言固遵舊制，然今日之事與昔不同。」

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the Ministry of State to debate; Gao Qi and others submitted: "What Xingxin said indeed follows old regulations, yet today's affair differs from former times."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the matter back to the ministry. Gao Qi replied: "Xingxin cites old practice, but times have changed."

sentences.zh: 詔姑待之。

translations.literal: An edict said to wait for now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a deferral.

sentences.zh: 已而高汝礪亦上言先遣使不便，議遂寢，語在汝礪傳。

translations.literal: Soon Gao Ruli also submitted that sending envoys first was inconvenient—the proposal then lapsed; the account is in Ruli's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli then argued against prior envoys and the plan died—the account is in his biography.

sentences.zh: 時監察禦史多被的決，行信乃上言曰：「大定間，監察坐罪大抵收贖，或至奪俸，重則外降而已，間有的決者，皆有為而然。

translations.literal: Then investigating censors were often rod-punished; Xingxin submitted: "During Dading, censors convicted of crime mostly paid redemption, or even salary confiscation; serious cases merely demotion outside the capital; occasionally rod punishment—always for cause.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censors were often flogged on the spot. Xingxin said: "Under Dading, censorial offenders usually paid fines, lost salary, or were demoted; flogging was rare and always for cause.

sentences.zh: 當時執政程輝已嘗面論其非是，又有敕旨，監察職主彈劾，而或看循者，非謂凡失察皆然也。

translations.literal: Then the chief minister Cheng Hui had already argued face-to-face that this was wrong; there was also an edict: censors' duty is impeachment, and laxity at times—not that every failure of oversight is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Cheng Hui had denounced this in person, and an edict had said censorial laxity in impeachment—not every oversight failure warranted flogging.

sentences.zh: 近日無問事之大小、情之輕重，一概的決，以為大定故實、先朝明訓，過矣。」

translations.literal: Recently regardless of affair's size or gravity of circumstance, all uniformly rod-punished—treating this as Dading precedent and former court's clear instruction—this goes too far."
translations.idiomatic: Lately every offense, great or small, is flogged on the spot as "Dading practice" and "former instruction"—that goes too far."

sentences.zh: 於是詔尚書省更定監察罪名制。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of State to re-fix censorial crime penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry was ordered to revise censorial penalties.

sentences.zh: 史館修《章宗實錄》，尚書省奏：「舊制，凡修史，宰相執政皆預焉。

translations.literal: The Historiography Institute compiled the Veritable Records of Zhangzong; the Ministry of State submitted: "Old regulation: whenever history is compiled, chief ministers in power all participate.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling Zhangzong's Veritable Records, the ministry reported: "By old rule, every history project includes the ruling chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 然女直、漢人各一員。

translations.literal: However one Jurchen and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: One Jurchen and one Han official each.

sentences.zh: 崇慶中，既以參知政事梁絪兼之，複命翰林承旨張行簡同事，蓋行簡家學相傳，多所考據。

translations.literal: In Chongqing, after making participation grand councilor Liang Yin concurrent, Hanlin Academician Zhang Xingjian was also ordered to join—the reason being Xingjian's hereditary family learning with much textual verification.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongqing, vice councilor Liang Yin was assigned and Academician Zhang Xingjian joined him—Xingjian came from a scholarly house and brought strong research.

sentences.zh: 今修《章宗實錄》，左丞汝礪已充兼修，宜令參知政事行信同修如行簡例。」

translations.literal: Now compiling the Veritable Records of Zhangzong, left vice councilor Ruli already serves as concurrent compiler—it is fitting to order participation grand councilor Xingxin to co-compile as in Xingjian's precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Ruli already co-compiles Zhangzong's records; Xingxin should join as Xingjian did."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，出為彰化軍節度使，兼涇州管內觀察使，諭之曰：「初，朕以朝臣多稱卿才，乃令參決機務。

translations.literal: Second year second month, sent out as military commissioner of Zhanghua Army, also observation commissioner within Jing Prefecture; instructed: "At first, I because many court ministers praised your talent made you participate in deciding state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two he was sent out as commissioner of Zhanghua and observer of Jing Prefecture. The emperor said: "Many praised your talent, so I brought you into council.

sentences.zh: 而廷議之際，每不據正，妄為異同，甚非為相之道。

translations.literal: Yet at court debate you each time did not hold to the correct, recklessly differing—very much not the way of serving as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in debate you constantly strayed from principle and argued for argument's sake—that is no way to serve as minister.

sentences.zh: 複聞邇來殊不以幹當為意，豈欲求散地故耶？

translations.literal: Also heard that recently you especially do not take diligence as your aim—do you perhaps wish for a remote post for that reason?
translations.idiomatic: I also hear you have been negligent—do you seek a quiet post?

sentences.zh: 今授此職，卿宜悉之。」

translations.literal: Now granting this post—you should fully understand."
translations.idiomatic: This post is yours; understand my meaning."

sentences.zh: 初，內族合周避敵不擊，且詭言密奉朝旨，下獄當誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, the imperial clan member He Zhou avoided the enemy without striking, and moreover falsely claimed secretly to obey court orders—imprisoned, liable for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, clansman He Zhou had fled the enemy and falsely claimed secret imperial orders—he was jailed and faced death.

sentences.zh: 諸皇族多抗表乞從末減，高琪以為自古犯法無告免者，行信獨曰：「事無古今，但合周平昔忠孝，或可以免。」

translations.literal: Many of the imperial clan submitted memorials resisting, begging mitigation; Gao Qi thought that from antiquity lawbreakers had none who pleaded exemption; Xingxin alone said: "Affairs have no ancient or modern—only that He Zhou in ordinary times was loyal and filial—perhaps he may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen petitioned for leniency. Gao Qi said criminals never escape by pleading. Xingxin alone said: "Antiquity matters less than his past loyalty and filial piety—mercy may be warranted."

sentences.zh: 又以行信族弟行貞居山東，受紅襖賊偽命，樞密院得宋人書，有干涉行信事，故出之。

translations.literal: Also because Xingxin's clansman younger brother Xingzhen dwelt in Shandong, accepting the Red Coats bandits' false appointment; the Bureau of Military Affairs obtained a Song letter with matter implicating Xingxin—therefore he was sent out.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xingzhen in Shandong had taken office under the Red Coats; the Bureau of Military Affairs found a Song letter implicating Xingxin—that is why he was sent out.

sentences.zh: 其子莒，時為尚書省令史，亦命別加注授焉。

translations.literal: His son Ju, then a Ministry of State clerk, was also ordered separately registered for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ju, a ministry clerk, was registered for appointment elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 初，行信言：「今法，職官論罪，多從的決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xingxin said: "Present law, when officials are sentenced for crime, mostly follows rod punishment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingxin had said: "Under current law, official crimes are mostly punished with on-the-spot flogging.

sentences.zh: 伏見大定間世宗敕旨，職官犯故違聖旨，徒年、杖數並的決。

translations.literal: I observe Shizong's edict during Dading: officials violating an edict in deliberate breach—years of penal servitude and rod strokes all on-the-spot.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's Dading edict said deliberate defiance of imperial orders meant flogging on the spot for labor and rod terms alike.

sentences.zh: 然其後三十餘年，有司論罪，未嘗引用，蓋非經久為例之事也。

translations.literal: Yet the thirty-plus years after, sentencing offices never cited it—surely not a matter of long-standing precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years afterward, no office cited it—it was never enduring precedent.

sentences.zh: 乞詳定之。」

translations.literal: I beg detailed fixing."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be clarified."

sentences.zh: 行信既出，上以其章付尚書省。

translations.literal: After Xingxin went out, the emperor gave his memorial to the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingxin's dismissal, the emperor sent his memorial to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 至是，宰臣奏：「自今違奏條之所指揮、及諸條格，當坐違制旨者，其徒年、杖數論贖可也。

translations.literal: At this time chief ministers submitted: "From now violations of commands in memorial provisions and various statutes that should incur violation of imperial decree—the penal servitude years and rod strokes may be commuted by redemption.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers proposed: "Henceforth violation of statutory commands may be redeemed—servitude terms and rod strokes included.

sentences.zh: 特奉詔旨違者，依大定例。」

translations.literal: Those specifically violating edict-orders—follow Dading precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate defiance of edicts would still follow the Dading rule."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 行信去未久，上嘗諭宰臣曰：「自張行信降黜，卿等遂緘默，此殊非是。

translations.literal: Not long after Xingxin left, the emperor once instructed chief ministers: "Since Zhang Xingxin was demoted, you then fell silent—this is very wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Xingxin's demotion, the emperor told his ministers: "Since Zhang Xingxin was demoted, you have fallen silent—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 行信事，卿等具知，豈以言之故耶！

translations.literal: Xingxin's affair—you all fully know—surely not because of speaking!
translations.idiomatic: You know Xingxin's case well—it is not because he spoke out!

sentences.zh: 自今宜各盡言，毋複畏忌。」

translations.literal: From now each should fully speak—no further fear and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth speak freely—without fear."

sentences.zh: 行信始至涇，即上書曰：「馬者甲兵之本，方軍旅未息，馬政不可緩也。

translations.literal: Xingxin upon first reaching Jing immediately submitted: "Horses are the root of armor and weapons—while armies have not ceased, horse policy cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jing, Xingxin immediately wrote: "Horses are the foundation of arms; while war continues, horse policy cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 臣自到涇，聞陝右豪民多市於河州，轉入內地，利蓋百倍。

translations.literal: Your servant since arriving at Jing has heard that Shaanxi-right powerful families mostly purchase at He Prefecture, transfer into the interior—the profit perhaps a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Since my arrival I hear Shaanxi magnates buy horses at He Prefecture and resell inland at enormous profit.

sentences.zh: 及見省差買馬官平涼府判官烏古論桓端市於洮州，以銀百鋌幾得馬千疋，雲生羌木波諸部蕃族人戶畜牧甚廣。

translations.literal: And seeing the provincially dispatched horse-buying officer Pingliang prefectural judge Wanyan Huanduan purchase at Tao Prefecture—with a hundred ingots of silver nearly obtaining a thousand horses—he said the Sheng Qiang, Mubo and various tribal Tibetan households' herding is very extensive.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial buyer Wanyan Huanduan at Tao Prefecture spent a hundred silver ingots and nearly got a thousand horses—the Sheng Qiang, Mubo, and other Tibetan tribes raise vast herds.

sentences.zh: 蓋前所遣官或抑其直，或以勢陵奪，遂失其和，且常患銀少，所以不能多得也。

translations.literal: Formerly dispatched officers perhaps suppressed prices, or by power bullied and seized—thus losing their good will, and always troubled by too little silver—so they could not obtain many.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier buyers lowballed prices or seized by force, alienating tribes and lacking silver—so yields were poor.

sentences.zh: 又聞蕃地今秋薄收，鬻馬得銀輒以易粟。

translations.literal: Also heard the tribal lands this autumn had poor harvests—selling horses for silver they promptly exchange for grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal lands had a poor harvest; sellers trade silver for grain at once.

sentences.zh: 冬春之交必艱食，馬價甚低。

translations.literal: At the winter-spring transition they must face food hardship—horse prices very low.
translations.idiomatic: By winter and spring they will be hungry—horse prices will be very low.

sentences.zh: 乞令所司輦銀粟於洮、河等州，選委知蕃情、達時變如桓端者貿易之。

translations.literal: I beg order the offices to transport silver and grain to Tao, He and other prefectures, select and commission those knowing tribal conditions and understanding timely changes like Huanduan to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Send silver and grain to Tao, He, and similar prefectures and appoint men like Huanduan who know the tribes and read the seasons to trade.

sentences.zh: 若捐銀萬兩，可得良馬千疋，機會不可失，惟朝廷亟圖之。」

translations.literal: If ten thousand taels of silver are spent, a thousand fine horses may be obtained—the opportunity cannot be lost; may the court urgently plan it."
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand taels could buy a thousand good horses—this chance must not be missed; I urge immediate action."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「此者沿邊戰士有功，朝廷遺使宣諭，賜以官賞，莫不感戴聖恩，願出死力，此誠得激勸之方也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Regarding this—border warriors with merit, the court sends envoys to announce and instruct, bestowing office and reward—all none fail to feel the holy grace and wish to give their utmost in death—this is truly the method of inspiring encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Meritorious border fighters receive imperial envoys, rewards, and offices—they gratefully pledge their lives. That truly inspires them.

sentences.zh: 然贈遺使者或馬或金，習以為常，臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: Yet presenting gifts to envoys—horses or gold—treated as custom—your servant has not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet gifting envoys horses or gold has become routine—I do not understand why.

sentences.zh: 大定間，嘗立送宣禮，自五品以上各有定數，後竟停罷。

translations.literal: During Dading, sending-announcement gifts were once established—from fifth rank up each had fixed amounts—later they were entirely halted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dading, announcement gifts were fixed by rank for fifth grade and above—then abolished.

sentences.zh: 況今時務與昔不同，而六品以下及止遷散官者，亦不免饋獻，或莫能辦，則斂所部以應之，至有因而獲罪者。

translations.literal: Moreover present affairs differ from former times, yet sixth rank down and those holding only provisional scattered offices also cannot escape tribute—some unable to provide then levy their subordinates to meet it—some even consequently convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Times have changed, yet sixth rank and below—and men with only provisional ranks—must still give gifts; some levy their districts and face punishment for it.

sentences.zh: 彼軍士效死立功，僅蒙恩賞，而反以饋獻為苦，是豈朝廷之意哉。

translations.literal: Those soldiers who risk death for merit barely receive grace and reward—yet suffer from tribute as hardship—is this the court's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Men who risk death for merit barely receive reward, then suffer mandatory gifts—is that the court's intent?

sentences.zh: 乞令有司依大定例，參以時務，明立等夷，使取予有限，無傷大體，則上下兩得矣。」

translations.literal: I beg order the offices according to Dading precedent, consulting present affairs, clearly establish grades, so taking and giving have limits without harming great principle—then above and below both gain."
translations.idiomatic: Restore Dading limits, adapted to present needs, so gifts are bounded and honor preserved—benefiting all."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「近聞保舉縣令，特增其俸，此朝廷為民之善意也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Recently heard that for recommended county magistrates, their salary is specially increased—this is the court's good intent for the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I hear recommended county magistrates have received higher salaries—a worthy intent to serve the people.

sentences.zh: 然自關以西，尚未有到任者，遠方之民不能無望。

translations.literal: Yet from the Pass westward, none have yet arrived to take office—the distant people's hope cannot be without.
translations.idiomatic: Yet west of the Pass none have taken up posts—distant subjects still wait.

sentences.zh: 豈舉者猶寡，而有所不敷耶？

translations.literal: Is it that recommenders are still few, and something is insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Are recommendations too few, or funds insufficient?

sentences.zh: 乞詔內外職事官，益廣選舉，以補其闕，使天下均受其賜。

translations.literal: I beg decree inner and outer officeholders to broaden selection to fill the gaps, so all under Heaven equally receive the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Order officials everywhere to broaden recommendations and fill vacancies so all the realm shares the benefit.

sentences.zh: 且丞、簿、尉亦皆親民，而獨不增俸，彼既不足以自給，安能禁其侵牟乎。

translations.literal: Moreover assistants, clerks, and constables also all are close to the people—yet alone their salary is not increased—they already insufficient for self-support—how can we forbid their extortion?
translations.idiomatic: Assistants, clerks, and constables serve the people too, yet their pay was not raised—they cannot live honestly without extortion.

sentences.zh: 或謂國用方闕，不宜虛費，是大不然。

translations.literal: Some say state revenue is deficient and empty expenditure is unsuitable—this is greatly not so.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the treasury is empty and this would waste funds—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫重吏祿者，固使之不擾民也，民安則國定，豈為虛費。

translations.literal: To weight officials' salary is precisely to make them not disturb the people—people at peace then state is stable—how is it empty waste?
translations.idiomatic: Higher salaries keep officials from harassing the people; secure subjects make a secure state—not waste.

sentences.zh: 誠能裁減冗食，不養無用之人，亦何患乎不足。

translations.literal: If truly able to cut redundant consumption, not maintain useless persons—what worry of insufficiency?
translations.idiomatic: Cut needless expenditures and idle mouths—and insolvency need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 今一軍充役，舉家廩給，軍既物故，給其子弟，感悅士心，為國盡力耳。

translations.literal: Now one soldier enters service—the whole family receives grain rations; when the soldier dies, his sons and younger brothers receive them—to move and please soldiers' hearts, that they exhaust strength for the state—that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Today one soldier enlists and the whole household is fed; when he dies, his brothers inherit the rations—that wins loyalty and strength for the state.

sentences.zh: 至於無男丁而其妻女猶給之，此何謂耶？

translations.literal: As for no adult males yet wives and daughters still receive rations—what does this mean?
translations.idiomatic: Yet rations continue to widows and daughters where no men remain—what sense is that?

sentences.zh: 自大駕南巡，存贍者已數年，張頤待哺，以困農民。

translations.literal: Since the imperial progress south, those sustained already several years—gaping mouths awaiting feeding, to burden the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's southern progress, dependents have been fed for years—mouths waiting to be fed, draining the farmers.

sentences.zh: 國家糧儲，常患不及，顧乃久養此老幼數千萬口，冗食虛費，正在是耳。

translations.literal: The state's grain stores constantly fear insufficiency—yet long maintaining these old and young tens of millions of mouths—redundant consumption and empty waste—precisely lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries always run short, yet millions of idle mouths are fed for years—that is the true waste.

sentences.zh: 如即罷之，恐其失所，宜限以歲月，使自為計，至期而罷，複將何辭。」

translations.literal: If immediately abolished, fear they lose their place—it is fitting to limit by months and years, let them plan for themselves—when the term ends and it is abolished, what further plea?"
translations.idiomatic: Abrupt cuts would leave them destitute; set a deadline so they can prepare—when it expires, they will have no complaint."

sentences.zh: 上多採納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 元光元年正月，遷保大軍節度使，兼鄜州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanguang he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Baoda Army, also Observation Commissioner within Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yuanguang (1222) he became military commissioner of Baoda Army and observation commissioner within Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二月，改靜難軍節度使，兼邠州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second month he was changed to Military Commissioner of Jingnan Army, also Observation Commissioner within Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he became military commissioner of Jingnan Army and observation commissioner within Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired.

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，徵用舊人，起為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Aizong took the throne he recalled old servants and raised Xingxin as Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong took the throne he recalled old servants and appointed Xingxin left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 言事稍不及前，人望頗減。

translations.literal: His memorials were somewhat less than before and public esteem declined.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were somewhat weaker than before and public esteem declined.

sentences.zh: 尋複致仕家居，惟以抄書教子孫為事，葺園池汴城東，築亭號「靜隱」，時時與侯摯輩遊詠其間。

translations.literal: Soon he retired again to live at home, only copying books to teach his sons and grandsons as his work; he repaired a garden pond east of Bianjing and built a pavilion called "Quiet Seclusion," often roaming and composing poetry there with Hou Zhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired again, living at home and copying books to teach his descendants. He laid out a garden east of Bianjing and built a pavilion called "Quiet Seclusion," often visiting it with Hou Zhi and others to compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 正大八年二月乙丑，薨於嵩山崇福宮，年六十有九。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the second month of the eighth year of Zhengda he died at Chongfu Palace on Mount Song, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the second month of the eighth year of Zhengda (1231) he died at Chongfu Palace on Mount Song, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初遊嵩山，嘗曰：「吾意欲主此山。」

translations.literal: When he first visited Mount Song he once said: "My intent is to make this mountain my home."
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to Mount Song he said: "I mean to make this mountain my home."

sentences.zh: 果終於此。

translations.literal: He did indeed end there.
translations.idiomatic: He did indeed end his days there.

sentences.zh: 為人純正真率，不事修飾，雖兩登相位，殆若無官然。

translations.literal: As a man he was pure, upright, and frank, not given to ornament; though twice reaching the chancellorship, he was almost as if without office.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure, upright, and frank, without affectation; though twice chancellor, he behaved almost as if he held no office.

sentences.zh: 遇事輒發，無所畏避，每奏事上前，旁人為動色，行信處之坦如也。

translations.literal: When matters arose he spoke out at once, fearing nothing; each time he reported before the throne others changed color, while Xingxin remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke out at once on every issue, fearing nothing. When he reported to the throne others paled while he remained calm.

sentences.zh: 及薨之日，雖平昔甚媢忌者，亦曰正人亡矣。

translations.literal: On the day he died, even those who had greatly envied him in ordinary times said a upright man is gone.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, even those who had envied him said an upright man was gone.

sentences.zh: 初至汴，父暐以御史大夫致仕，猶康健，兄行簡為翰林學士承旨，行信為禮部尚書，諸子侄多中第居官，當世未之有也。

translations.literal: When he first reached Bianjing, his father Wei had retired as Censor-in-Chief and was still healthy; his elder brother Xingjian was Hanlin Academician Expositor; Xingxin was Minister of Rites; many sons and nephews passed examinations and held office—the age had not seen the like.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached Bianjing, his father Wei had retired as censor-in-chief and was still healthy; his brother Xingjian was Hanlin expositor; Xingxin was minister of rites; many sons and nephews held degrees and office—unmatched in their day.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高汝礪禔身清慎，練達事宜，久居相位，雖為大夫士所鄙，而人主寵遇不衰。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gao Ruli cultivated himself in purity and caution, was practiced in affairs, long held the chancellorship—though despised by great officers and scholars, the ruler's favor never waned.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Gao Ruli was pure and cautious, skilled in affairs, and long held the chancellorship. Though despised by scholar-officials, the ruler's favor never waned.

sentences.zh: 張行信礪志謇諤，言無避忌，然一簉政途，便多坎壈，及其再用，論事稍不及前，豈以汝礪為真可法耶。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingxin sharpened his will in blunt remonstrance and spoke without avoidance; yet once he entered the political path he met many setbacks, and when employed again his discussion was somewhat less than before—was Ruli truly to be taken as a model?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingxin was resolute and blunt, speaking without fear; yet once in office he met many setbacks, and when recalled his counsel was weaker—was Ruli truly a model?

sentences.zh: 宣宗伐宋，本非萬全之策，行信諫，汝礪不諫，又沮和議。

translations.literal: Xuanzong's campaign against Song was never a plan of complete security—Xingxin remonstrated, Ruli did not, and moreover blocked peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong's war on Song was never a sure plan—Xingxin remonstrated, Ruli did not, and blocked peace talks.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎之惡未著，行信兩疏擊之。

translations.literal: Before Hu Shahu's wickedness was manifest, Xingxin twice memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hu Shahu's wickedness was manifest, Xingxin twice memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 汝礪與高琪共事，人疑其黨附。

translations.literal: Ruli served with Gao Qi and people suspected partisan attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Ruli served with Gao Qi and people suspected partisan loyalty.

sentences.zh: 優劣可概見於斯矣。

translations.literal: Their relative merit and fault may be seen in summary here.
translations.idiomatic: Their relative merit may be seen in summary here.
